```{r hmm-combined-behavior-gps-map-pasture-filtered, fig.width=14, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
        color = "grey35",
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = active_shapes,
        fill = NA,
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 1
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = map_points_inside,
        aes(color = Behavior),
        alpha = 0.42,
        size = 0.8
      ) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Grazing" = "#2E8B57","Resting" = "#4169E1","Walking" = "#E76F51")) +
      facet_wrap(~Rotation_Label) +
      coord_sf(
        xlim = c(pasture_bbox["xmin"], pasture_bbox["xmax"]),
        ylim = c(pasture_bbox["ymin"], pasture_bbox["ymax"]),
        datum = NA,
        expand = FALSE
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(group_name, "— all behaviors"),
        subtitle = paste(
          nrow(map_points_inside),
          "GPS observations within the pasture;",
          "black outline identifies the active grazing area"
        ),
        color = "Behavior"
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()
      )
  })

```


### 4.8 Create Separate Maps for Each Behavior

The following chunk creates an independent map series for **Grazing**, **Resting**, and **Walking**. Within each behavior map, the rotation periods remain in separate panels. This makes the spatial distribution of one behavior easier to examine without points from the other behavior classes.

```{r hmm-separate-behavior-maps-unfiltered, fig.width=14, fig.height=7.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
behavior_levels_to_map <- c("Grazing", "Resting", "Walking")

separate_behavior_map_list_unfiltered <- list()

for (group_name in unique(behavior_gps_sf$Map_Group)) {
  group_points <- behavior_gps_sf %>%
    filter(Map_Group == group_name)

  pasture_id <- unique(group_points$Pasture_ID)

  if (length(pasture_id) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected one pasture for map group: ", group_name)
  }

  background <- pasture_sf %>%
    filter(Pasture_ID == pasture_id)

  active_shapes <- active_period_sf %>%
    filter(Map_Group == group_name)

  for (behavior_name in behavior_levels_to_map) {
    behavior_points <- group_points %>%
      filter(Behavior == behavior_name)

    # Keep a map even when a behavior has no GPS records in one or more periods.
    map_key <- paste(group_name, behavior_name, sep = " — ")

    separate_behavior_map_list_unfiltered[[map_key]] <- ggplot() +
      geom_sf(
        data = background,
        fill = "grey96",
        color = "grey35",
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = active_shapes,
        fill = NA,
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 1.0
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = behavior_points,
        color = switch(
          behavior_name,
          "Grazing" = "#2E8B57",
          "Resting" = "#4169E1",
          "Walking" = "#E76F51",
          "black"
        ),
        alpha = 0.55,
        size = 0.85
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~ Rotation_Label, ncol = 3, drop = FALSE) +
      coord_sf(datum = NA) +
      labs(
        title = paste(group_name, "—", behavior_name),
        subtitle = paste(
          behavior_name,
          "GPS observations shown separately by rotation period"
        ),
        caption = "Black outline identifies the active grazing area for each period."
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
      )
  }
}

```


```{r hmm-separate-behavior-maps-pasture-filtered, fig.width=14, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
behavior_levels_to_map <- c("Grazing", "Resting", "Walking")

separate_behavior_map_list <- list()

for (group_name in unique(behavior_gps_sf$Map_Group)) {

  group_points <- behavior_gps_sf %>%
    filter(Map_Group == group_name)

  pasture_id <- unique(group_points$Pasture_ID)

  if (length(pasture_id) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected one pasture for map group: ", group_name)
  }

  background <- pasture_sf %>%
    filter(Pasture_ID == pasture_id)

  if (nrow(background) == 0L) {
    stop("No pasture polygon found for map group: ", group_name)
  }

  active_shapes <- active_period_sf %>%
    filter(Map_Group == group_name)

  # Transform spatial objects to the pasture CRS
  group_points <- st_transform(
    group_points,
    st_crs(background)
  )

  active_shapes <- st_transform(
    active_shapes,
    st_crs(background)
  )

  # Keep only GPS points inside or on the pasture boundary
  group_points_inside <- st_filter(
    group_points,
    background,
    .predicate = st_intersects
  )

  pasture_bbox <- st_bbox(background)

  for (behavior_name in behavior_levels_to_map) {

    behavior_points <- group_points_inside %>%
      filter(Behavior == behavior_name)

    map_key <- paste(
      group_name,
      behavior_name,
      sep = " — "
    )

    behavior_color <- switch(
      behavior_name,
      "Grazing" = "#2E8B57",
      "Resting" = "#4169E1",
      "Walking" = "#E76F51",
      "black"
    )

    separate_behavior_map_list[[map_key]] <- ggplot() +
      geom_sf(
        data = background,
        fill = "grey96",
        color = "grey35",
        linewidth = 0.7
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = active_shapes,
        fill = NA,
        color = "black",
        linewidth = 1
      ) +
      geom_sf(
        data = behavior_points,
        color = behavior_color,
        alpha = 0.55,
        size = 0.85
      ) +
      facet_wrap(
        ~Rotation_Label,
        ncol = 3,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      coord_sf(
        xlim = c(
          pasture_bbox["xmin"],
          pasture_bbox["xmax"]
        ),
        ylim = c(
          pasture_bbox["ymin"],
          pasture_bbox["ymax"]
        ),
        datum = NA,
        expand = FALSE
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(group_name, "—", behavior_name),
        subtitle = paste(
          nrow(behavior_points),
          behavior_name,
          "GPS observations within the pasture"
        ),
        caption = paste(
          "Black outline identifies the active grazing",
          "area for each period."
        )
      ) +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
      )
  }
}

```



## 5. Centralized Export of Results, Figures, and Maps

This section saves all HMM grazing-behavior and spatial outputs under one root
folder:
`params$output_dir/01_Grazing_Behavior_Spatial_Aera`.
Set `params$export_results` to `false` when a report preview is needed without
writing files. Existing files with the same names are replaced so a complete
rerun produces a synchronized results folder.

### 5.1 Create the Output Directory Structure

```{r hmm-initialize-output-directories}
# Keep every export from Sections 5.1-5.5 inside one folder.
# This intentionally overrides the earlier HMM output_root only for exporting.
output_root <- file.path(
  master_output_root,
  "01_Grazing_Behavior_Spatial_Aera"
)

output_dirs <- list(
  tables = file.path(output_root, "01_Tables"),
  models = file.path(output_root, "02_Model_Results"),
  figures = file.path(output_root, "03_Figures"),
  maps_qc_state = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "01_QC_State"),
  maps_final_state = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "02_Final_State"),
  maps_qc_combined = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "03_QC_Combined"),
  maps_final_combined = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "04_Final_Combined"),
  maps_qc_separate = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "05_QC_Separate"),
  maps_final_separate = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "06_Final_Separate"),
  maps_active_area = file.path(output_root, "04_Maps", "07_Active_Area"),
  spatial = file.path(output_root, "05_Spatial_Data")
)

# Folders are created only when their final outputs are written.

safe_file_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_") %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all("^_+|_+$", "") %>%
    stringr::str_to_lower()
}

message(
  "Section 5 export root: ",
  normalizePath(output_root, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
)
```

### 5.2 Save Analysis Tables

Derived datasets are written to CSV. The publication-style
`Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors` table is retained here for the first worksheet of
`06_Statistical_Analysis/01_Tables/AFRI_Statistical_Results.xlsx`. It reports the
estimated marginal mean (EMM) ± SE for each Treatment x Stocking Rate
combination, Tukey compact-letter post hoc groups, and Type III P-values for
TRT, SR, and TRT x SR. The same workbook retains the cached numerical EMMs,
post hoc letters, comparisons, and complete reference ANOVA results for auditing.

```{r hmm-export-analysis-tables}
# Every object below is defined in Sections 1-4. No weekly table objects are
# defined upstream; do not reference them here.
derived_tables <- list(
  analysis_dataset = dat_all,
  daily_distance = Daily_DDT,
  monthly_distance = Monthly_DDT,
  monthly_distance_filtered = Monthly_DDT_filtered,
  daily_behavior_minutes = behavior_time,
  daily_behavior_hours = behavior_hours,
  daily_behavior_hours_wide = behavior_hours_wide,
  daily_behavior_hours_qc = behavior_hours_wide_qc,
  excluded_behavior_days = excluded_days,
  grazing_monthly = df.Grazing_monthly,
  resting_monthly = df.Resting_monthly,
  traveling_monthly = df.Traveling_monthly,
  grazing_monthly_flagged = df.Grazing_monthly_flagged,
  resting_monthly_flagged = df.Resting_monthly_flagged,
  traveling_monthly_flagged = df.Traveling_monthly_flagged,
  grazing_monthly_filtered = df.Grazing_monthly_filtered,
  resting_monthly_filtered = df.Resting_monthly_filtered,
  traveling_monthly_filtered = df.Traveling_monthly_filtered,
  rotation_schedule = behavior_rotation_schedule,
  behavior_gps_by_rotation = behavior_gps,
  map_period_index = map_period_index,
  active_area_summary = active_area_summary,
  whole_season_active_area_summary = season_active_summary,
  whole_season_map_index = season_map_index,
  gps_active_area_lookup = gps_active_area_lookup
)

anova_to_data_frame <- function(model) {
  result <- as.data.frame(afri_reference_anova(model))
  result$Effect <- rownames(result)
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  result[, c("Effect", setdiff(names(result), "Effect")), drop = FALSE]
}

format_table_p <- function(p) {
  if (length(p) == 0L || is.na(p) || !is.finite(p)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  if (p < 0.001) {
    return("<0.001")
  }
  sprintf("%.3f", p)
}

extract_type3_p <- function(model, effect_names) {
  tab <- as.data.frame(afri_reference_anova(model))
  tab$Effect <- rownames(tab)
  rownames(tab) <- NULL

  p_col <- grep("^Pr\\(", names(tab), value = TRUE)[1]
  if (is.na(p_col)) {
    stop("Could not identify the P-value column in car::Anova output.")
  }

  idx <- which(tab$Effect %in% effect_names)
  if (length(idx) == 0L) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  as.numeric(tab[[p_col]][idx[1]])
}

# Models used for the table shown in the manuscript-style layout.
# These are the four behavior/movement models fitted earlier in this file.
table1_models <- list(
  "Grazing (h/day)" = mod.Monthly_Grazing,
  "Resting (h/day)" = mod.Monthly_Resting,
  "Traveling (h/day)" = mod.Monthly_Traveling,
  "Daily distance traveled (km/day)" = mod.Monthly_DDT_filtered
)

cell_levels <- c(
  "Continuous Light",
  "Continuous Moderate",
  "Continuous Heavy",
  "Rotational Light",
  "Rotational Moderate",
  "Rotational Heavy"
)

build_table1_component <- function(model, variable_label) {
  # These EMM grids were already computed from the same retained fit.
  existing_emms <- list(
    "Grazing (h/day)" = emm.Monthly_Grazing,
    "Resting (h/day)" = emm.Monthly_Resting,
    "Traveling (h/day)" = emm.Monthly_Traveling,
    "Daily distance traveled (km/day)" = emm_DDT
  )
  emm_object <- existing_emms[[variable_label]]
  if (is.null(emm_object)) stop("No retained EMM grid for ", variable_label)

  cld_df <- as.data.frame(
    multcomp::cld(
      emm_object,
      Letters = letters,
      adjust = "tukey"
    )
  )

  estimate_col <- intersect(
    c("response", "emmean", "prob", "rate"),
    names(cld_df)
  )[1]

  if (is.na(estimate_col)) {
    stop(
      "Could not identify the EMM estimate column for ",
      variable_label,
      "."
    )
  }

  lower_col <- intersect(
    c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"),
    names(cld_df)
  )[1]

  upper_col <- intersect(
    c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"),
    names(cld_df)
  )[1]

  cld_df <- cld_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Variable = variable_label,
      TRT = as.character(TRT),
      SR = as.character(SR),
      PostHoc_Letter = stringr::str_squish(.group),
      EMM = as.numeric(.data[[estimate_col]]),
      SE = as.numeric(SE),
      Cell = paste(TRT, SR),
      Display = sprintf(
        "%.2f ± %.2f %s",
        EMM,
        SE,
        PostHoc_Letter
      )
    )

  p_trt <- extract_type3_p(model, "TRT")
  p_sr <- extract_type3_p(model, "SR")
  p_int <- extract_type3_p(model, c("TRT:SR", "SR:TRT"))

  wide_emm <- cld_df %>%
    dplyr::select(Variable, Cell, Display) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = Cell,
      values_from = Display
    )

  for (nm in cell_levels) {
    if (!nm %in% names(wide_emm)) {
      wide_emm[[nm]] <- NA_character_
    }
  }

  summary_row <- wide_emm %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n = stats::nobs(model),
      `P: TRT` = format_table_p(p_trt),
      `P: SR` = format_table_p(p_sr),
      `P: TRT * SR` = format_table_p(p_int)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Variable,
      n,
      dplyr::all_of(cell_levels),
      `P: TRT`,
      `P: SR`,
      `P: TRT * SR`
    )

  long_emm <- cld_df %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Variable,
      n = stats::nobs(model),
      TRT,
      SR,
      EMM,
      SE,
      df = if ("df" %in% names(cld_df)) as.numeric(df) else NA_real_,
      Lower_95CI = if (!is.na(lower_col)) as.numeric(.data[[lower_col]]) else NA_real_,
      Upper_95CI = if (!is.na(upper_col)) as.numeric(.data[[upper_col]]) else NA_real_,
      PostHoc_Letter
    )

  list(
    summary = summary_row,
    emm_posthoc = long_emm,
    anova = anova_to_data_frame(model)
  )
}

table1_results <- lapply(
  names(table1_models),
  function(variable_label) {
    build_table1_component(
      table1_models[[variable_label]],
      variable_label
    )
  }
)

names(table1_results) <- names(table1_models)

Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(table1_results, function(x) x$summary)
)

Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors_EMM_PostHoc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  lapply(table1_results, function(x) x$emm_posthoc)
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    TRT = factor(TRT, levels = c("Continuous", "Rotational")),
    SR = factor(SR, levels = c("Light", "Moderate", "Heavy"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Variable, TRT, SR) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    TRT = as.character(TRT),
    SR = as.character(SR)
  )

inferential_tables <- list(
  Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors = Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors,
  Table_1_EMM_PostHoc = Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors_EMM_PostHoc,
  Grazing_ANOVA = anova_to_data_frame(mod.Monthly_Grazing),
  Resting_ANOVA = anova_to_data_frame(mod.Monthly_Resting),
  Traveling_ANOVA = anova_to_data_frame(mod.Monthly_Traveling),
  DDT_ANOVA = anova_to_data_frame(mod.Monthly_DDT_filtered)
)

if (export_results) {
  dir.create(output_dirs$tables, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  expected_table_names <- names(derived_tables)
  message("Section 5.2: exporting ", length(expected_table_names),
          " upstream-derived datasets; Table 1 joins the final statistical workbook.")
  for (table_name in names(derived_tables)) {
    this_table <- derived_tables[[table_name]]
    if (!is.data.frame(this_table) && !inherits(this_table, "sf")) {
      warning("Skipping non-tabular export: ", table_name)
      next
    }
    if (inherits(this_table, "sf")) {
      this_table <- sf::st_drop_geometry(this_table)
    }
    readr::write_csv(
      this_table,
      file.path(
        output_dirs$tables,
        paste0(safe_file_name(table_name), ".csv")
      )
    )
  }

  readr::write_csv(
    tibble::tibble(
      Dataset = names(derived_tables),
      Rows = vapply(derived_tables, nrow, integer(1)),
      Columns = vapply(derived_tables, ncol, integer(1)),
      Export_File = paste0(vapply(names(derived_tables), safe_file_name,
                                   character(1)), ".csv")
    ),
    file.path(output_dirs$tables, "Exported_Datasets_Inventory.csv")
  )

  # Table 1 and its cached inference are exported once in the final
  # AFRI_Statistical_Results workbook; retain the protected objects in memory.
  message("Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors retained for the first sheet of AFRI_Statistical_Results.xlsx.")


}

Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors
```

### 5.3 Save Model Objects and Printed Results

The four models used in `Table_1_Grazing_Behaviors` are saved as RDS files for
exact reuse. A companion text file contains each model summary and its Type III
test table.

```{r hmm-export-model-results}
model_objects <- list(
  monthly_grazing = mod.Monthly_Grazing,
  monthly_resting = mod.Monthly_Resting,
  monthly_traveling = mod.Monthly_Traveling,
  monthly_ddt = mod.Monthly_DDT_filtered
)

if (export_results) {
  dir.create(output_dirs$models, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (model_name in names(model_objects)) {
    model <- model_objects[[model_name]]
    model_stem <- safe_file_name(model_name)

    saveRDS(
      model,
      file = file.path(
        output_dirs$models,
        paste0(model_stem, ".rds")
      )
    )

    model_report <- c(
      paste("MODEL:", model_name),
      paste(rep("=", 72), collapse = ""),
      capture.output(summary(model)),
      "",
      "TYPE III TESTS",
      paste(rep("-", 72), collapse = ""),
      capture.output(print(afri_reference_anova(model)))
    )

    writeLines(
      model_report,
      con = file.path(
        output_dirs$models,
        paste0(model_stem, ".txt")
      )
    )
  }
}
```

### 5.4 Save Statistical Figures and Diagnostic Graphs

The four primary EMM figures are exported once as 300-dpi PNG files.
A two-panel residual diagnostic PNG is also saved for each Table 1 model.

```{r hmm-export-statistical-figures}
if (export_results) {
  dir.create(output_dirs$figures, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

primary_figures <- list(
  DDT_means = p_Avg_DDT,
  Grazing_means = p.Grazing,
  Resting_means = p.Resting,
  Traveling_means = p.Traveling
)

save_ggplot_figure <- function(
    plot_object,
    filename,
    width = 9,
    height = 6
) {
  png_file <- file.path(
    output_dirs$figures,
    paste0(filename, ".png")
  )


  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = png_file,
    plot = plot_object,
    device = safe_png_device,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )


}

save_model_diagnostic <- function(model, filename, label) {
  output_file <- file.path(
    output_dirs$figures,
    filename
  )

  safe_png_device(
    filename = output_file,
    width = 10,
    height = 5,
    units = "in",
    res = 300,
    bg = "white"
  )

  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(
    {
      par(old_par)
      grDevices::dev.off()
    },
    add = TRUE
  )

  model_resid <- residuals(model)
  model_fitted <- fitted(model)

  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

  qqnorm(
    model_resid,
    main = paste(label, "residual Q-Q")
  )
  qqline(model_resid, lwd = 2)

  plot(
    model_fitted,
    model_resid,
    xlab = "Fitted values",
    ylab = "Residuals",
    main = paste(label, "residuals vs fitted")
  )
  abline(h = 0, lwd = 2)

  invisible(output_file)
}

if (export_results) {
  for (figure_name in names(primary_figures)) {
    save_ggplot_figure(
      primary_figures[[figure_name]],
      safe_file_name(figure_name)
    )
  }

  save_model_diagnostic(
    mod.Monthly_Grazing,
    "diagnostic_grazing.png",
    "Grazing"
  )

  save_model_diagnostic(
    mod.Monthly_Resting,
    "diagnostic_resting.png",
    "Resting"
  )

  save_model_diagnostic(
    mod.Monthly_Traveling,
    "diagnostic_traveling.png",
    "Traveling"
  )

  save_model_diagnostic(
    mod.Monthly_DDT_filtered,
    "diagnostic_daily_distance.png",
    "Daily distance"
  )

  message(
    "Figures exported to: ",
    normalizePath(
      output_dirs$figures,
      winslash = "/",
      mustWork = FALSE
    )
  )
}
```

```{r hmm-export-map-images-and-spatial-layers}
    nchar(representative_png),
    " characters long. If PNG export fails on Windows, move the project ",
    "closer to the drive root while keeping the same output folder name."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. VERIFIED PNG EXPORT HELPERS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

save_verified_png <- function(
    plot,
    filename,
    width,
    height,
    dpi = 300,
    bg = "white"
) {

  if (!export_results) return(invisible(NULL))
  target_filename <- filename
  directory <- dirname(target_filename)
  dir.create(directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  if (!dir.exists(directory)) stop("Could not create PNG output directory: ", directory)
  temporary_png <- tempfile(pattern = "afri-map-", tmpdir = directory, fileext = ".png")
  filename <- temporary_png
  on.exit(if (file.exists(temporary_png)) unlink(temporary_png), add = TRUE)
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Primary PNG writer
  #
  # Do NOT use safe_png_device here. The previous code allowed
  # ggsave() to return without guaranteeing that the requested
  # target file actually existed. Use the standard PNG device
  # and verify the exact target immediately.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  primary_error <- NULL

  tryCatch(
    {
      ggplot2::ggsave(
        filename = filename,
        plot = plot,
        device = "png",
        width = width,
        height = height,
        units = "in",
        dpi = dpi,
        bg = bg,
        limitsize = FALSE
      )
    },
    error = function(e) {
      primary_error <<- conditionMessage(e)
    }
  )

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Fallback: direct grDevices::png()
  #
  # This avoids any custom device wrapper and writes directly
  # to the requested file.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  file_ok <- is.null(primary_error) && file.exists(filename)

  if (file_ok) {
    file_size <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(file.info(filename)$size)
    )

    file_ok <- is.finite(file_size) && file_size > 0
  }

  if (!file_ok) {

    if (file.exists(filename)) {
      unlink(filename, force = TRUE)
    }

    direct_error <- NULL

    tryCatch(
      {
        grDevices::png(
          filename = filename,
          width = width,
          height = height,
          units = "in",
          res = dpi,
          bg = bg
        )

        print(plot)

        grDevices::dev.off()
      },
      error = function(e) {

        direct_error <<- conditionMessage(e)

        # Close only an open graphics device.
        if (grDevices::dev.cur() > 1L) {
          try(
            grDevices::dev.off(),
            silent = TRUE
          )
        }
      }
    )

    file_ok <- is.null(direct_error) && file.exists(filename)

    if (file_ok) {
      file_size <- suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(file.info(filename)$size)
      )

      file_ok <- is.finite(file_size) && file_size > 0
    }

    if (!file_ok) {
      stop(
        "PNG export failed for:\n",
        filename,
        "\nPrimary ggsave error: ",
        ifelse(
          is.null(primary_error),
          "<ggsave returned but target file was absent/empty>",
          primary_error
        ),
        "\nDirect png() fallback error: ",
        ifelse(
          is.null(direct_error),
          "<png() returned but target file was absent/empty>",
          direct_error
        )
      )
    }
  }

  final_size <- as.numeric(
    file.info(filename)$size
  )

  message(
    "PNG created: ",
    basename(filename),
    " (",
    format(final_size, big.mark = ","),
    " bytes)"
  )

  if (!file.copy(filename, target_filename, overwrite = TRUE)) {
    stop("Could not save verified PNG: ", target_filename)
  }
  filename <- target_filename

  invisible(filename)
}


save_map_collection <- function(
    plot_list,
    directory,
    width,
    height
) {

  if (
    is.null(plot_list) ||
      length(plot_list) == 0L
  ) {
    return(invisible(character(0)))
  }

  if (
    is.null(names(plot_list)) ||
      any(names(plot_list) == "")
  ) {
    stop(
      "Map collection contains missing/blank map names."
    )
  }

  dir.create(
    directory,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )

  if (!dir.exists(directory)) {
    stop(
      "Could not create map directory: ",
      directory
    )
  }

  output_files <- character(
    length(plot_list)
  )

  for (i in seq_along(plot_list)) {

    map_name <- names(plot_list)[i]

    output_file <- file.path(
      directory,
      paste0(
        safe_file_name(map_name),
        ".png"
      )
    )

    output_files[i] <- save_verified_png(
      plot = plot_list[[i]],
      filename = output_file,
      width = width,
      height = height,
      dpi = 300,
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  names(output_files) <- names(plot_list)

  invisible(output_files)
}



# ============================================================
# 2. CLEAN SF OBJECT BEFORE GEOPACKAGE EXPORT
# ============================================================

clean_sf_for_gpkg <- function(
    x,
    layer_name,
    qc_directory = NULL
) {

  if (!inherits(x, "sf")) {
    stop(
      layer_name,
      " is not an sf object."
    )
  }


  if (nrow(x) == 0L) {

    warning(
      layer_name,
      " contains zero rows."
    )

    return(x)
  }


  message(
    "\nPreparing spatial layer: ",
    layer_name
  )

  message(
    "Rows before cleaning: ",
    format(
      nrow(x),
      big.mark = ","
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Keep original row number for QC
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  x$.export_original_row <-
    seq_len(
      nrow(x)
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Check duplicate field names ignoring case
  #
  # GeoPackage uses SQLite, where field-name conflicts can
  # occur even if R considers names different by capitalization.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  geom_column <-
    attr(
      x,
      "sf_column"
    )


  attribute_names <-
    setdiff(
      names(x),
      geom_column
    )


  duplicated_case_names <-
    duplicated(
      tolower(
        attribute_names
      )
    )


  if (any(duplicated_case_names)) {

    duplicated_names <-
      attribute_names[
        duplicated_case_names
      ]

    stop(
      "Duplicate GeoPackage attribute names detected in ",
      layer_name,
      ": ",
      paste(
        duplicated_names,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  }


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean attribute columns
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  attribute_columns <-
    setdiff(
      names(x),
      c(
        geom_column,
        ".export_original_row"
      )
    )


  for (nm in attribute_columns) {

    z <- x[[nm]]


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # factor -> character
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (is.factor(z)) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        as.character(z)

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # POSIXlt -> POSIXct
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (inherits(z, "POSIXlt")) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        as.POSIXct(z)

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # difftime / hms -> numeric seconds
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (
      inherits(z, "difftime") ||
        inherits(z, "hms")
    ) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        as.numeric(z)

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # bit64::integer64
    #
    # Character preserves exact IDs better than converting
    # large IDs to floating-point numeric.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (inherits(z, "integer64")) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        as.character(z)

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # logical -> integer
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (is.logical(z)) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        as.integer(z)

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Clean character encoding
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (is.character(z)) {

      x[[nm]] <-
        iconv(
          z,
          from = "",
          to = "UTF-8",
          sub = ""
        )

      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Replace NaN / Inf / -Inf in numeric attributes with NA
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (is.numeric(z)) {

      bad_numeric <-
        !is.na(z) &
        !is.finite(z)


      if (any(bad_numeric)) {

        message(
          "  ",
          layer_name,
          ": replacing ",
          sum(bad_numeric),
          " non-finite value(s) with NA in ",
          nm
        )


        z[bad_numeric] <- NA_real_

        x[[nm]] <- z
      }


      next
    }


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # List columns are problematic in GeoPackage tables.
    # Convert them to text rather than allowing GDAL to fail.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (is.list(z)) {

      message(
        "  ",
        layer_name,
        ": converting list column '",
        nm,
        "' to character."
      )


      x[[nm]] <-
        vapply(
          z,

          function(value) {

            if (
              is.null(value) ||
                length(value) == 0L ||
                all(is.na(value))
            ) {

              return(NA_character_)
            }


            paste(
              as.character(
                unlist(value)
              ),
              collapse = ";"
            )
          },

          FUN.VALUE =
            character(1)
        )


      next
    }
  }



  # ==========================================================
  # Geometry QC
  # ==========================================================

  geometry <-
    sf::st_geometry(x)


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Empty geometries
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  empty_geometry <-
    sf::st_is_empty(
      geometry
    )


  empty_geometry[
    is.na(empty_geometry)
  ] <- TRUE



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Validity check
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  valid_geometry <-
    suppressWarnings(
      sf::st_is_valid(
        geometry,
        NA_on_exception = TRUE
      )
    )


  bad_validity <-
    is.na(valid_geometry)



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Explicit non-finite coordinate check
  #
  # This catches POINT(NaN NaN), Inf coordinates, etc.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  finite_geometry <-
    vapply(

      geometry,

      function(g) {

        values <-
          suppressWarnings(
            as.numeric(
              unlist(g)
            )
          )


        if (length(values) == 0L) {
          return(FALSE)
        }


        all(
          is.finite(values)
        )
      },

      FUN.VALUE =
        logical(1)
    )



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Rows that cannot safely be exported
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  bad_geometry <-
    empty_geometry |
    bad_validity |
    !finite_geometry



  if (any(bad_geometry)) {

    n_bad <-
      sum(
        bad_geometry
      )


    warning(
      layer_name,
      " contains ",
      n_bad,
      " invalid/empty/non-finite geometry row(s). ",
      "They will be excluded from the GeoPackage export."
    )


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Save bad rows for QC
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    bad_rows <-
      sf::st_drop_geometry(
        x[
          bad_geometry,
          ,
          drop = FALSE
        ]
      )


    bad_rows$Export_QC_reason <-
      paste0(

        ifelse(
          empty_geometry[bad_geometry],
          "EMPTY_GEOMETRY;",
          ""
        ),

        ifelse(
          bad_validity[bad_geometry],
          "INVALID_GEOMETRY;",
          ""
        ),

        ifelse(
          !finite_geometry[bad_geometry],
          "NONFINITE_COORDINATE;",
          ""
        )
      )


    if (!is.null(qc_directory)) {

      dir.create(
        qc_directory,
        recursive = TRUE,
        showWarnings = FALSE
      )


      readr::write_csv(

        bad_rows,

        file.path(
          qc_directory,
          paste0(
            safe_file_name(layer_name),
            "__DROPPED_EXPORT_ROWS.csv"
          )
        )
      )
    }


    x <-
      x[
        !bad_geometry,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
  }



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Drop Z/M dimensions if present.
  #
  # The analysis uses planar XY geometry; unnecessary Z/M
  # dimensions can create export compatibility problems.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  x <-
    tryCatch(

      sf::st_zm(
        x,
        drop = TRUE,
        what = "ZM"
      ),

      error =
        function(e) {
          x
        }
    )



  message(
    "Rows after geometry QC: ",
    format(
      nrow(x),
      big.mark = ","
    )
  )


  x
}



# ============================================================
# 3. SAFE GEOPACKAGE WRITER
# ============================================================

write_gpkg_safe <- function(
    x,
    dsn,
    layer,
    chunk_size = 100000L,
    qc_directory = NULL
) {
  if (!export_results) return(invisible(NULL))

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean layer
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  x <-
    clean_sf_for_gpkg(

      x = x,

      layer_name = layer,

      qc_directory =
        qc_directory
    )



  if (nrow(x) == 0L) {

    warning(
      "Skipping ",
      layer,
      ": zero valid rows after export QC."
    )

    return(
      invisible(NULL)
    )
  }



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Make destination directory
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  destination_directory <-
    dirname(
      dsn
    )


  dir.create(
    destination_directory,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )


  if (!dir.exists(destination_directory)) {

    stop(
      "Could not create spatial output directory: ",
      destination_directory
    )
  }



  target_dsn <- dsn
  temporary_gpkg <- tempfile("afri-spatial-", tmpdir = destination_directory,
                             fileext = ".gpkg")
  dsn <- temporary_gpkg
  on.exit(if (file.exists(temporary_gpkg)) unlink(temporary_gpkg), add = TRUE)

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Number of chunks
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  n <-
    nrow(x)


  chunk_size <-
    as.integer(
      chunk_size
    )


  starts <-
    seq.int(
      from = 1L,
      to = n,
      by = chunk_size
    )



  message(
    "\nWriting GeoPackage layer: ",
    layer
  )

  message(
    "Destination: ",
    dsn
  )

  message(
    "Features: ",
    format(
      n,
      big.mark = ","
    )
  )

  message(
    "Chunks: ",
    length(starts)
  )



  # ==========================================================
  # Write chunks
  # ==========================================================

  for (
    chunk_number in
    seq_along(starts)
  ) {

    first_row <-
      starts[
        chunk_number
      ]


    last_row <-
      min(
        first_row +
          chunk_size -
          1L,
        n
      )


    message(
      "  Chunk ",
      chunk_number,
      "/",
      length(starts),
      ": rows ",
      format(
        first_row,
        big.mark = ","
      ),
      "-",
      format(
        last_row,
        big.mark = ","
      )
    )



    chunk <-
      x[
        first_row:last_row,
        ,
        drop = FALSE
      ]



    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # First chunk creates the GeoPackage
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    if (chunk_number == 1L) {

      sf::st_write(

        obj =
          chunk,

        dsn =
          dsn,

        layer =
          layer,

        driver =
          "GPKG",

        append =
          FALSE,

        delete_layer =
          TRUE,

        quiet =
          FALSE,

        layer_options =
          "SPATIAL_INDEX=NO"
      )



    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Remaining chunks append
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    } else {

      sf::st_write(

        obj =
          chunk,

        dsn =
          dsn,

        layer =
          layer,

        driver =
          "GPKG",

        append =
          TRUE,

        quiet =
          FALSE
      )
    }
  }



  # ==========================================================
  # Verify written layer
  # ==========================================================

  layer_info <-
    sf::st_layers(
      dsn
    )


  if (
    !layer %in%
      layer_info$name
  ) {

    stop(
      "GeoPackage was written but expected layer was not found: ",
      layer
    )
  }



  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Verify feature count WITHOUT reading the spatial layer
  # back into memory. st_layers() already reports the feature
  # count and avoids duplicating a large sf object in RAM.
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  layer_index <-
    match(
      layer,
      layer_info$name
    )

  written_count <-
    suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(
        layer_info$features[
          layer_index
        ]
      )
    )


  if (
    !is.na(written_count) &&
      written_count != n
  ) {

    stop(
      "GeoPackage feature-count mismatch for ",
      layer,
      ". Expected ",
      n,
      " rows but found ",
      written_count,
      "."
    )
  }


  if (is.na(written_count)) {
    warning(
      "GeoPackage layer was created, but GDAL did not report a ",
      "feature count for ",
      layer,
      ". The layer-existence check passed."
    )
  }



  message(
    "SUCCESS: ",
    layer,
    " — ",
    format(
      written_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),
    " features written."
  )


  if (!file.copy(dsn, target_dsn, overwrite = TRUE)) {
    stop("Could not save verified GeoPackage: ", target_dsn)
  }
  dsn <- target_dsn

  invisible(
    dsn
  )
}



# ============================================================
# 4. EXPORT EVERYTHING
# ============================================================

if (export_results) {


  # ==========================================================
  # MAPS
  # ==========================================================

  save_map_collection(
    behavior_gps_map_list_unfiltered,
    output_dirs$maps_qc_state,
    width = 15,
    height = 9
  )


  save_map_collection(
    behavior_gps_map_list,
    output_dirs$maps_final_state,
    width = 14,
    height = 8
  )


  save_map_collection(
    behavior_gps_combined_map_list_unfiltered,
    output_dirs$maps_qc_combined,
    width = 14,
    height = 8
  )


  save_map_collection(
    behavior_gps_combined_map_list,
    output_dirs$maps_final_combined,
    width = 14,
    height = 8
  )


  save_map_collection(
    separate_behavior_map_list_unfiltered,
    output_dirs$maps_qc_separate,
    width = 14,
    height = 7.5
  )


  save_map_collection(
    separate_behavior_map_list,
    output_dirs$maps_final_separate,
    width = 14,
    height = 8
  )



  # ==========================================================
  # ACTIVE-AREA GRID MAPS
  # ==========================================================

  save_map_collection(

    stats::setNames(
      active_area_map_list,
      paste0(
        "01_ALL_PASTURE__",
        names(
          active_area_map_list
        )
      )
    ),

    output_dirs$maps_active_area,

    width = 14,

    height = 8
  )



  save_map_collection(

    stats::setNames(
      inside_rgp_area_map_list,
      paste0(
        "02_INSIDE_RGP__",
        names(
          inside_rgp_area_map_list
        )
      )
    ),

    output_dirs$maps_active_area,

    width = 14,

    height = 8
  )



  # Whole-season export must contain one PNG per Year x Pasture.
  expected_whole_season_map_names <- season_map_index$Season_Map_Group

  if (
    length(
      whole_season_area_map_list
    ) != length(
      expected_whole_season_map_names
    ) ||
      !setequal(
        names(
          whole_season_area_map_list
        ),
        expected_whole_season_map_names
      )
  ) {
    stop(
      "Whole-season map export failed QC: map-list names do not ",
      "match the expected Year x Pasture groups."
    )
  }


  # Existing obsolete files are left untouched. Only current named outputs are written.

  whole_season_export_inventory <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(
      seq_len(
        nrow(season_map_index)
      ),
      function(i) {

        y <- as.integer(
          season_map_index$Year[i]
        )

        p <- as.integer(
          season_map_index$Pasture_ID[i]
        )

        group_name <- sprintf(
          "%d_Pasture_%d",
          y,
          p
        )

        map_object <- whole_season_area_map_list[[group_name]]

        if (
          is.null(
            map_object
          )
        ) {
          stop(
            "Missing whole-season map object for ",
            group_name,
            "."
          )
        }

        output_file <- file.path(
          output_dirs$maps_active_area,
          sprintf(
            "03_whole_season_%d_pasture_%d.png",
            y,
            p
          )
        )

        output_file <- save_verified_png(
          plot = map_object,
          filename = output_file,
          width = 10,
          height = 8,
          dpi = 300,
          bg = "white"
        )

        tibble::tibble(
          Year = y,
          Pasture_ID = p,
          File = output_file,
          Exists = file.exists(output_file),
          Bytes = as.numeric(file.info(output_file)$size)
        )
      }
    )
  )


  whole_season_export_inventory <- whole_season_export_inventory %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Exists = file.exists(File),
      Bytes = vapply(
        File,
        function(z) {
          if (!file.exists(z)) {
            return(NA_real_)
          }

          as.numeric(
            file.info(z)$size
          )
        },
        numeric(1)
      ),
      Valid_PNG =
        Exists &
        is.finite(Bytes) &
        Bytes > 0
    )

  print(
    whole_season_export_inventory
  )

  failed_whole_season_png <- whole_season_export_inventory %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !Valid_PNG
    )

  if (nrow(failed_whole_season_png) > 0L) {

    print(
      failed_whole_season_png
    )

    stop(
      "One or more Year x Pasture whole-season PNG files were ",
      "not created correctly. The failed exact paths are printed above."
    )
  }


  if (
    anyDuplicated(
      basename(
        whole_season_export_inventory$File
      )
    )
  ) {
    stop(
      "Duplicate whole-season output filenames were generated."
    )
  }



  # ==========================================================
  # RELEASE FINISHED MAP OBJECTS BEFORE SPATIAL EXPORT
  # ==========================================================
  #
  # ggplot objects can retain references to large sf/GPS data.
  # Once the PNG files above have been written, these map lists
  # are no longer needed downstream. Removing them here reduces
  # peak RAM before GeoPackage export and the overview maps.
  # ==========================================================

  map_objects_to_release <- intersect(
    c(
      "behavior_gps_map_list_unfiltered",
      "behavior_gps_map_list",
      "behavior_gps_combined_map_list_unfiltered",
      "behavior_gps_combined_map_list",
      "separate_behavior_map_list_unfiltered",
      "separate_behavior_map_list",
      "active_area_map_list",
      "inside_rgp_area_map_list",
      "whole_season_area_map_list"
    ),
    ls(envir = .GlobalEnv)
  )

  if (length(map_objects_to_release) > 0L) {
    rm(
      list = map_objects_to_release,
      envir = .GlobalEnv
    )
  }

  rm(map_objects_to_release)
  invisible(gc(full = TRUE))

  message(
    "Finished exporting HMM map collections and released ",
    "their ggplot objects from memory."
  )


  # ==========================================================
  # SPATIAL LAYERS
  # ==========================================================

  dir.create(
    output_dirs$spatial,
    recursive = TRUE,
    showWarnings = FALSE
  )


  spatial_layers <- list(

    pasture_polygons =
      pasture_sf,

    rotation_polygons =
      rotation_sf,

    active_period_polygons =
      active_period_sf,

    behavior_gps_points =
      behavior_gps_sf,

    active_grazing_grid =
      active_grazing_grid_sf,

    all_pasture_active_grid =
      all_pasture_active_grid_sf,

    inside_RGP_active_grid =
      inside_RGP_active_grid_sf,

    gps_active_area_geometry =
      gps_active_area_geometry_sf
  )



  # ==========================================================
  # WRITE EACH LAYER TO ITS OWN GPKG
  # ==========================================================

  spatial_export_results <-
    vector(
      mode = "list",
      length =
        length(
          spatial_layers
        )
    )


  names(
    spatial_export_results
  ) <-
    names(
      spatial_layers
    )



  for (
    layer_name in
    names(
      spatial_layers
    )
  ) {


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # GPS data are much larger, so use smaller chunks.
    #
    # Other spatial layers can use larger chunks.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    this_chunk_size <-
      if (
        layer_name ==
          "behavior_gps_points"
      ) {

        25000L

      } else {

        100000L
      }



    output_gpkg <-
      file.path(
        output_dirs$spatial,
        paste0(
          safe_file_name(layer_name),
          ".gpkg"
        )
      )



    spatial_export_results[[layer_name]] <-
      tryCatch(

        {

          write_gpkg_safe(

            x =
              spatial_layers[[layer_name]],

            dsn =
              output_gpkg,

            layer =
              layer_name,

            chunk_size =
              this_chunk_size,

            qc_directory =
              output_dirs$spatial
          )


          list(
            Layer =
              layer_name,

            Status =
              "SUCCESS",

            File =
              output_gpkg,

            Error =
              NA_character_
          )
        },


        error =
          function(e) {


            message(
              "\n========================================"
            )

            message(
              "\nFAILED SPATIAL EXPORT: ",
              layer_name
            )

            message(
              "\n",
              conditionMessage(e)
            )

            message(
              "\n========================================\n"
            )


            list(
              Layer =
                layer_name,

              Status =
                "FAILED",

              File =
                output_gpkg,

              Error =
                conditionMessage(e)
            )
          }
      )

    # Release temporary copies created while cleaning/writing
    # each sf layer before moving to the next layer.
    invisible(gc(full = FALSE))
  }



  # ==========================================================
  # SPATIAL EXPORT SUMMARY
  # ==========================================================

  spatial_export_summary <-
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      lapply(

        spatial_export_results,

        function(x) {

          tibble::tibble(

            Layer =
              x$Layer,

            Status =
              x$Status,

            File =
              x$File,

            Error =
              x$Error
          )
        }
      )
    )



  print(
    spatial_export_summary
  )



  readr::write_csv(

    spatial_export_summary,

    file.path(
      output_dirs$spatial,
      "Spatial_export_summary.csv"
    )
  )



  # ==========================================================
  # FINAL FAILURE WARNING
  # ==========================================================

  failed_layers <-
    spatial_export_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Status != "SUCCESS"
    )


  if (nrow(failed_layers) > 0L) {

    warning(
      "One or more spatial layers failed to export. ",
      "See Spatial_export_summary.csv and console messages."
    )
  }
}
```

# 2. Grazing Body Weight and Spatial Production


## Analysis Overview

This master R Markdown workflow imports and cleans three years of steer body-weight data, performs exploratory and smooth-spline analyses, fits an inferential mixed-effects model, and evaluates spatial production efficiency. The document is organized in execution order so that every derived object is created before it is used.

The numbered hierarchy follows the format **section → subsection → procedure** (for example, 1, 1.2, and 1.2.1). Code chunks use unique descriptive labels, and comments identify the purpose, assumptions, validation checks, and principal output objects. Paths for source data and GIS inputs should be reviewed before rendering the document in a new computing environment.

The final section creates a reproducible output package containing:

- quality-control, exploratory, spline, inferential, production, and spatial result tables;
- serialized model and analysis objects;
- all figures generated while rendering the report;
- a separate collection of map images and spatial data files; and
- a manifest and R session-information file for traceability.

## 1. Data Loading

### 1.1 Configure the R Environment

Load all the necessary R packages that will be used for data manipulation, visualization, modeling, and evaluation. The installation commands are commented out, assuming the packages are already installed.

```{r bw-setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# the additional worksheet-reading and functional-iteration packages here.

library(purrr)

  "pasture_sf", "rotation_sf", "pasture_feature_map", "ranch_shapefile",
  "rotation_shapefiles", "ranch_source_crs", "rotation_source_crs", "spatial_analysis_crs")
if (!all(vapply(bw_spatial_input_names, function(nm) exists(nm, inherits = TRUE), logical(1)))) {
  stop("Run the preceding HMM/GPS spatial preparation chunks before this section.")
}
bw_spatial_cache <- mget(bw_spatial_input_names, inherits = TRUE)

# Unit-conversion constants used throughout the analysis.

# hectares.

# and logs create their destination only when an output is written.

bw_steer_workbook <- as.character(params$bw_steer_workbook)
if (!grepl("^(/|[A-Za-z]:[/\\\\])", bw_steer_workbook)) {

}

  master_output_root,

)

  tables = file.path(analysis_output_root, "01_Tables"),
  models = file.path(analysis_output_root, "02_Model_Results"),
  figures = file.path(analysis_output_root, "03_Figures"),

)

bw_ensure_output_parent <- function(path) {
  dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

}
# Knitr needs its figure parent during execution; other folders are created
```

#### 1.1.1 Define Reusable Data-Preparation Functions

```{r bw-helper-functions}
# -------------------------------
# Shorten all AnimalTag numbers to 6 digits
# -------------------------------

SubstrRight <- function(x, n){
  substr(x, nchar(x)-n+1, nchar(x))
}

# -------------------------------
# Function to add a leading zero if the ID has 5 digits 
# -------------------------------

add_zero <- function(id) {
  if (nchar(id) == 5) {
    id <- paste0("0", id)
  }
  return(id)
}

# -------------------------------
# Function to fix Excel date serial numbers in column names
# -------------------------------

fix_date_colnames <- function(df) {
  old_names <- names(df)
  
  # Date columns start after Year, so columns 7 to the end
  date_cols <- 7:length(old_names)
  
  old_names[date_cols] <- format(
    as.Date(as.numeric(old_names[date_cols]), origin = "1899-12-30"),
    "%m/%d/%Y"
  )
  
  names(df) <- old_names
  return(df)
}

# -------------------------------
# Reshape Smart Scale datasets
# -------------------------------

reshape_smart_scale <- function(df, year_label) {
  df %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = matches("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"),  # Select columns formatted as YYYY-MM-DD
      names_to = "Date",                         # Move date column names into one Date column
      values_to = "BW"                        # Store Smart Scale body weights
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Date = as.Date(Date),                      # Convert Date to proper Date format
      Year = year_label                          # Add year identifier
    )
}

# -------------------------------
# Reshape steer body information and weight datasets
# -------------------------------

reshape_steers <- function(df, year_label) {
  df %>%
    # Convert all date columns to numeric BW values before reshaping.
    # This prevents pivot_longer() errors when one date column is read as numeric
    # and another date column is read as character.
    mutate(across(
      matches("^\\d{2}/\\d{2}/\\d{4}$"),
      ~ readr::parse_number(as.character(.x))
    )) %>%
    
    # Reshape from wide format to long format
    pivot_longer(
      cols = matches("^\\d{2}/\\d{2}/\\d{4}$"),
      names_to = "Date",
      values_to = "BW"
    ) %>%
    
    # Convert the date column to Date format and add year
    mutate(
      Date = as.Date(Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"),
      Year = year_label
    )
}

```

#### 1.3.1 Impute the Documented 2023 Missing Value

Check data sets for missing values to ensure data quality.

```{r bw-missing-value-imputation}
# The steer is missing body weight (BW) for 09/03/2023.
# Because the animal has a BW recorded on the next day, 09/04/2023,
# the missing value on 09/03/2023 is replaced with the 09/04/2023 value.
# This assumes the steer’s BW was effectively the same across those two consecutive days.
Steers_2023 <- Steers_2023 %>%
  mutate(`09/03/2023` = ifelse(
    is.na(`09/03/2023`),
    `09/04/2023`,
    `09/03/2023`
  ))

cat("Missing values in Steers_2023:\n")
print(colSums(is.na(Steers_2023)))
```


## 2. Data Preparation and Integration

This section converts all yearly files to a consistent long format, standardizes animal identifiers and data types, merges experimental assignments into the Smart Scale records, and combines all sources into one multi-year analysis dataset. Validation checks are retained immediately after each consequential transformation.

### 2.2 Clean and Standardize Animal Identification Numbers

```{r bw-clean-and-standardize-animal-identifiers}
# This step prepares the yearly Smart Scale and steer datasets for later analysis.
# The datasets are cleaned separately per each year instead of using the combined datasets.
#
# For the Smart Scale datasets:
# 1. Remove the Name column.
# 2. Remove records where BW is 0.0, because these values do not represent valid body weights.
# 3. Rename RFIDTag to SEID so it matches the steer body weight datasets.
# 4. Shorten SEID values to the last 6 digits using the SubstrRight() function.
#
# For the steer body weight and steer information datasets:
# 1. Convert SEID to character format.
# 2. Add a leading zero to SEID values that only have 5 digits using the add_zero() function.

# -------------------------------
# Clean Smart Scale datasets per each year
# -------------------------------

df_SS_2023_long <- df_SS_2023_long %>%
  dplyr::select(-Name) %>%
  filter(BW != 0.0) %>%
  rename(SEID = RFIDTag) %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = SubstrRight(SEID, 6)
  )

df_SS_2024_long <- df_SS_2024_long %>%
  dplyr::select(-Name) %>%
  filter(BW != 0.0) %>%
  rename(SEID = RFIDTag) %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = SubstrRight(SEID, 6)
  )

df_SS_2025_long <- df_SS_2025_long %>%
  dplyr::select(-Name) %>%
  filter(BW != 0.0) %>%
  rename(SEID = RFIDTag) %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = SubstrRight(SEID, 6)
  )


# -------------------------------
# Clean steer body weight datasets per each year
# -------------------------------

Steers_2023_long <- Steers_2023_long %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
  )

Steers_2024_long <- Steers_2024_long %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
  )

Steers_2025_long <- Steers_2025_long %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
  )



# -------------------------------
# Clean steer information datasets per each year
# -------------------------------

Steers_2023_info <- Steers_2023_info %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
  )

Steers_2024_info <- Steers_2024_info %>%
  mutate(
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
  )

Steers_2025_info <- Steers_2025_info %>%
  mutate(

    SEID = unname(sapply(SEID, add_zero))
```

```{r bw-verify-smart-scale-information-merge}
# -------------------------------
# Create formatted unmatched SEID report
# -------------------------------

# This function prints the total number of unmatched unique SEIDs
# and lists the SEID values. If no unmatched SEIDs are found, it prints "None".

print_unmatched_report <- function(year, unmatched_data) {
  
  unmatched_seids <- sort(unique(unmatched_data$SEID))
  total_unmatched <- length(unmatched_seids)
  
  cat("\n", year, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("Total unmatched:", total_unmatched, "\n")
  
  if (total_unmatched == 0) {
    cat("SEID: None\n")
  } else {
    cat("SEID:", paste(unmatched_seids, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
}

print_unmatched_report(2025, unmatched_SS_2025)
```

## 3. Exploratory Data Analysis

The exploratory workflow uses one daily observation per animal, prioritizes manual measurements when both sources occur on the same animal-date, evaluates coverage and experimental allocation, summarizes body-weight distributions and trajectories, and documents observations excluded from spline fitting. Exclusion rules are kept explicit so that all removals remain auditable.

The exploratory analysis below uses the planned grazing periods only:

- 2023: June 5 through August 27 (82 calendar days)
- 2024: June 5 through August 25 (81 calendar days)
- 2025: June 5 through August 24 (82 calendar days)

Body weight is converted from pounds to kilograms before this analysis. Before interpreting treatment or stocking-rate differences, remember that treatments are applied to pastures. Therefore, pasture—not each daily animal observation—is the experimental unit for treatment-level inference. The analyses in this section are descriptive and are intended to reveal data quality, coverage, patterns, and potential anomalies.

### 3.1 Create the EDA Analysis Dataset

```{r bw-eda-analysis-dataset, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Define the analysis window for each year.
analysis_windows <- tibble(
  Year = c(2023, 2024, 2025),
  Start_Date = as.Date(c("2023-06-05", "2024-06-05", "2025-06-05")),
  End_Date   = as.Date(c("2023-08-27", "2024-08-25", "2025-08-27"))
) %>%
  mutate(Expected_Days = as.integer(End_Date - Start_Date) + 1L)

# Restrict the combined data to the requested periods and create aligned study days.
BW_EDA <- BW_combined %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(as.character(Year))) %>%
  inner_join(analysis_windows, by = "Year") %>%
  filter(Date >= Start_Date, Date <= End_Date) %>%
  mutate(
    Day_of_Study = as.integer(Date - Start_Date) + 1L,
    Year = factor(Year, levels = c(2023, 2024, 2025)),
    Pasture = factor(Pasture, levels = as.character(1:6)),
    TRT = factor(TRT),
    SR = factor(SR),
    BW_Source = factor(BW_Source, levels = c("Manual", "Smart Scale")),
    Animal_ID = interaction(Year, SEID, drop = TRUE, sep = "-")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

# Basic verification of the date restriction.
BW_EDA %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    First_Date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Last_Date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Expected_Days = first(Expected_Days),
    Observed_Dates = n_distinct(Date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### 3.2 Data Integrity and Experimental-Design Checks

#### 3.2.1 Missing Values and Invalid Records

```{r bw-eda-missing-integrity}
missing_summary <- tibble(
  Variable = names(BW_EDA),
  Missing_n = vapply(BW_EDA, function(x) sum(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
  Missing_percent = round(
    100 * vapply(BW_EDA, function(x) mean(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
    2
  )
)

missing_summary

# Records with missing or nonpositive BW should be reviewed.
invalid_bw_records <- BW_EDA %>%
  filter(is.na(BW) | !is.finite(BW) | BW <= 0)

cat("Number of missing, non-finite, or nonpositive BW records:",
    nrow(invalid_bw_records), "\n")
invalid_bw_records
```

#### 3.2.2 Duplicate Animal-Date Records

A duplicate may occur if a manual and Smart Scale weight are both retained for the same animal and date. The duplicate report is printed before creating a one-record-per-animal-per-day dataset. When both sources occur on the same date, the manual measurement is retained for the descriptive daily dataset.

```{r bw-eda-duplicates}
animal_day_duplicates <- BW_EDA %>%
  count(Year, SEID, Date, name = "Records_per_animal_day") %>%
  filter(Records_per_animal_day > 1) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

cat("Animal-date combinations with more than one record:",
    nrow(animal_day_duplicates), "\n")
animal_day_duplicates

# Create a single daily value for each animal.
# Manual BW receives priority only when both data sources occur on the same date.
BW_daily <- BW_EDA %>%
  mutate(
    Source_priority = case_when(
      BW_Source == "Manual" ~ 1L,
      BW_Source == "Smart Scale" ~ 2L,
      TRUE ~ 3L
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date, Source_priority) %>%
  group_by(Year, SEID, Date) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-Source_priority)

stopifnot(
  BW_daily %>% count(Year, SEID, Date) %>% summarise(max_n = max(n)) %>% pull(max_n) == 1
)
```

#### 3.2.3 Animal Allocation by Year, Pasture, Treatment, and Stocking Rate

```{r bw-eda-design-counts}
# One row per animal within year.
animal_assignments <- BW_daily %>%
  distinct(Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR)

# Number of animals in each experimental group.
design_counts <- animal_assignments %>%
  count(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture, name = "Animals") %>%
  arrange(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture)

design_counts

# Check whether each pasture has a single treatment and stocking-rate assignment.
pasture_assignment_check <- animal_assignments %>%
  group_by(Year, Pasture) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Number_of_TRT_values = n_distinct(TRT),
    TRT_values = paste(sort(unique(as.character(TRT))), collapse = ", "),
    Number_of_SR_values = n_distinct(SR),
    SR_values = paste(sort(unique(as.character(SR))), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Pasture)

pasture_assignment_check

# Any row returned here indicates an assignment inconsistency within a pasture-year.
pasture_assignment_check %>%
  filter(Number_of_TRT_values != 1 | Number_of_SR_values != 1)
```

### 3.3 Observation Coverage and Completeness

```{r bw-eda-coverage-summary}
year_coverage <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Planned_Start = first(Start_Date),
    Planned_End = first(End_Date),
    Expected_Days = first(Expected_Days),
    First_Observed_Date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Last_Observed_Date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Days_with_any_BW = n_distinct(Date),
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Observations = n(),
    Expected_animal_days = Animals * Expected_Days,
    Completeness_percent = round(100 * Observations / Expected_animal_days, 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

year_coverage

animal_coverage <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    First_Date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Last_Date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Days_observed = n_distinct(Date),
    Expected_Days = first(Expected_Days),
    Completeness_percent = round(100 * Days_observed / Expected_Days, 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Completeness_percent, Pasture, SEID)

animal_coverage

# Animals with less than 90% of planned daily records.
animal_coverage %>%
```

### 3.6 Longitudinal Body-Weight Patterns

#### 3.6.1 Daily Treatment and Stocking-Rate Means

```{r bw-eda-daily-group-trajectories, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
daily_group_summary <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year, Day_of_Study, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Mean_BW = mean(BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BW = sd(BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_BW = SD_BW / sqrt(Animals),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  daily_group_summary,
  aes(x = Day_of_Study, y = Mean_BW, color = TRT, fill = TRT, group = TRT)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Mean_BW - SE_BW, ymax = Mean_BW + SE_BW),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(Year ~ SR, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Daily Body-Weight Trajectories",
    subtitle = "Ribbon represents mean ± one descriptive standard error",
    x = "Day of study",
    y = "Mean body weight (kg)",
    color = "Treatment",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

#### 3.6.2 Pasture-Level Trajectories

```{r bw-eda-pasture-trajectories, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
daily_pasture_summary <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year, Day_of_Study, Pasture, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Mean_BW = mean(BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_BW = sd(BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  daily_pasture_summary,
  aes(x = Day_of_Study, y = Mean_BW, color = Pasture, group = Pasture)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Year, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Pasture-Level Daily Mean Body Weight",
    x = "Day of study",
    y = "Mean body weight (kg)",
    color = "Pasture"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
