### 3.7 Outlier and Abrupt-Change Screening

The following flags are diagnostic only. A flagged value should be checked against source records and animal history before it is changed or removed.

#### 3.7.1 Extreme BW Values Within Year

```{r bw-eda-bw-outlier-flags}
# Use wide Tukey limits (3 × IQR) to flag only very extreme yearly values.
yearly_bw_limits <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Q1 = quantile(BW, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(BW, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    Lower_limit = Q1 - 3 * IQR,
    Upper_limit = Q3 + 3 * IQR,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

extreme_bw_records <- BW_daily %>%
  left_join(yearly_bw_limits, by = "Year") %>%
  filter(BW < Lower_limit | BW > Upper_limit) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, Date, Day_of_Study, Tag, SEID, Pasture, TRT, SR,
         BW_Source, BW, Lower_limit, Upper_limit) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

cat("Number of extreme BW records flagged:", nrow(extreme_bw_records), "\n")
extreme_bw_records
```

#### 3.7.2 Abrupt Within-Animal Daily Changes

```{r bw-eda-change-flags}
BW_changes <- BW_daily %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date) %>%
  group_by(Year, SEID) %>%
  mutate(
    Previous_Date = lag(Date),
    Previous_BW = lag(BW),
    Days_between = as.integer(Date - Previous_Date),
    BW_change_per_day = (BW - Previous_BW) / Days_between
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(BW_change_per_day), Days_between > 0)

# Calculate typical BW change within the same year, treatment, and
# stocking-rate group. This makes the outlier rule sensitive to unusual
# changes within groups such as Light stocking rate in 2024.
change_limits <- BW_changes %>%
  group_by(Year, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Median_change = median(BW_change_per_day, na.rm = TRUE),
    MAD_change = mad(BW_change_per_day, constant = 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# User-adjustable abrupt-change rules for 2024 Light only.
# Robust_distance is unitless; BW_change_per_day is in kg/day.
bw_change_mad_cutoff <- 4
max_bw_change_kg_per_day <- 20 * pounds_to_kilograms

abrupt_change_records <- BW_changes %>%
  left_join(change_limits, by = c("Year", "TRT", "SR")) %>%
  mutate(
    Robust_distance = if_else(
      MAD_change > 0,
      abs(BW_change_per_day - Median_change) / MAD_change,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    Year == 2024,
    SR == "Light",
    is.finite(Robust_distance),
    Robust_distance > bw_change_mad_cutoff,
    abs(BW_change_per_day) > max_bw_change_kg_per_day
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, Date, Tag, SEID, Pasture, TRT, SR,
         Previous_Date, Previous_BW, BW, Days_between,
         BW_change_per_day, Robust_distance) %>%
  arrange(Year, SR, TRT, desc(abs(BW_change_per_day)))

cat("Number of abrupt-change records flagged:",
    nrow(abrupt_change_records), "\n")
head(abrupt_change_records, 50)
```

#### 3.7.3 Remove Abrupt-Change Days Before Fitting Smooth Splines

The original `BW_daily` object is retained unchanged. The new object
`BW_daily_spline` removes flagged animal-days only from the 2024 Light
stocking-rate group. All observations from Heavy and Moderate stocking rates,
and all Light observations from other years, are retained. Within 2024 Light,
a day is removed when its BW change exceeds both four MAD units and
9.07 kg/day (equivalent to the original 20 lb/day criterion).
The original `BW_daily` object remains unchanged.

```{r bw-remove-abrupt-bw-days}
# Extreme BW animal-days identified in Section 3.7.1.
extreme_bw_days <- extreme_bw_records %>%
  transmute(
    Year,
    SEID,
    Date,
    Removal_reason = "Extreme yearly BW value"
  )

# Abrupt within-animal changes identified in Section 3.7.2.
abrupt_bw_days <- abrupt_change_records %>%
  transmute(
    Year,
    SEID,
    Date,
    Removal_reason = paste0(
      "Abrupt within-animal BW change: > ",
      bw_change_mad_cutoff,
      " MAD and > ",
      round(max_bw_change_kg_per_day, 2),
      " kg/day"
    )
  )

# Remove all BW observations from P3 during study days 50–70 in 2024.
p3_2024_days <- BW_daily %>%
  filter(
    Year == 2024,
    as.character(Pasture) == "3",
    between(Day_of_Study, 50, 70)
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Year,
    SEID,
    Date,
    Removal_reason = "P3 in 2024, study days 50–70"
  )

# Combine all removal rules.
# If one animal-day meets multiple rules, retain all applicable reasons.
bw_days_to_remove <- bind_rows(
  extreme_bw_days,
  abrupt_bw_days,
  p3_2024_days
) %>%
  distinct(Year, SEID, Date, Removal_reason) %>%
  group_by(Year, SEID, Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Removal_reason = paste(
      sort(unique(Removal_reason)),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

###################### IMPORTANT ####################
# Retain BW_daily as the raw dataset and create a cleaned spline dataset.
BW_daily_spline <- BW_daily %>%
  anti_join(
    bw_days_to_remove,
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Date")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

# Extract the complete records that were removed for inspection.
removed_bw_records <- BW_daily %>%
  inner_join(
    bw_days_to_remove,
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Date")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

# Summarize removals by reason.
bw_removal_by_reason <- bw_days_to_remove %>%
  separate_rows(Removal_reason, sep = "; ") %>%
  count(Year, Removal_reason, name = "Animal_days_removed") %>%
  arrange(Year, Removal_reason)

# Summarize the total number of unique observations removed by year.
bw_removal_summary <- bw_days_to_remove %>%
  count(Year, name = "Observations_removed") %>%
  right_join(
    BW_daily %>%
      count(Year, name = "Original_observations"),
    by = "Year"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Observations_removed = replace_na(Observations_removed, 0L),
    Remaining_observations =
      Original_observations - Observations_removed,
    Percent_removed = round(
      100 * Observations_removed / Original_observations,
      3
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year)

cat(
  "Total unique animal-days removed before spline fitting:",
  nrow(bw_days_to_remove),
  "\n"
)

bw_removal_summary
bw_removal_by_reason

# Display the removed 2024 P3 observations from days 50–70.
p3_2024_removed <- removed_bw_records %>%
  filter(
    Year == 2024,
    as.character(Pasture) == "3",
    between(Day_of_Study, 50, 70)
  )

cat(
  "P3 observations removed from study days 50–70 in 2024:",
  nrow(p3_2024_removed),
  "\n"
)

p3_2024_removed
```

### 3.8 Exploratory Animal-Level Growth Rates

An animal-specific linear slope provides a simple descriptive summary of change across the grazing period. It does not replace a repeated-measures or mixed-effects analysis, and it can be influenced by scale noise and missing days.

```{r bw-eda-animal-growth-rates}
animal_growth <- BW_daily %>%
  group_by(Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(Day_of_Study) >= 10) %>%
  summarise(
    Days_observed = n_distinct(Day_of_Study),
    Study_span_days = max(Day_of_Study) - min(Day_of_Study),
    First_BW = BW[which.min(Day_of_Study)],
    Last_BW = BW[which.max(Day_of_Study)],
    Observed_change = Last_BW - First_BW,
    Endpoint_ADG = if_else(
      Study_span_days > 0,
      Observed_change / Study_span_days,
      NA_real_
    ),
    Regression_ADG = if_else(
      var(Day_of_Study, na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
      cov(Day_of_Study, BW, use = "complete.obs") /
        var(Day_of_Study, na.rm = TRUE),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Linear_R_squared = cor(Day_of_Study, BW, use = "complete.obs")^2,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

animal_growth_summary <- animal_growth %>%
  group_by(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n(),
    Mean_Regression_ADG = mean(Regression_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Regression_ADG = sd(Regression_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Regression_ADG = median(Regression_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Endpoint_ADG = mean(Endpoint_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture)

animal_growth_summary
```

```{r bw-eda-animal-growth-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
ggplot(animal_growth, aes(x = TRT, y = Regression_ADG, fill = TRT)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.55) +
  facet_grid(Year ~ SR, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Exploratory Animal-Level Linear Growth Slopes",
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Regression slope (kg/day)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### 3.9 EDA Outputs to Retain for Later Modeling

The principal analysis-ready objects created above are:

- `BW_daily`: one body-weight record per animal per study day, restricted to the requested periods;
- `BW_daily_spline`: the spline-analysis dataset after removing abrupt-change animal-days;
- `animal_assignments`: animal allocation by year, pasture, treatment, and stocking rate;
- `year_coverage` and `animal_coverage`: data-completeness summaries;
- `extreme_bw_records` and `abrupt_change_records`: observations requiring source-data review;
- `animal_growth`: descriptive animal-level growth slopes.

For formal treatment comparisons, a later model should preserve the hierarchical and longitudinal structure of the study, including year, pasture, animal, and repeated day effects. Avoid treating all animal-day observations as independent replicates.


## 4. Smooth-Spline Body-Weight Analysis

This section fits one smooth spline per steer-year, generates daily fitted body weights and derivatives, derives animal-level growth metrics, evaluates residual behavior, and compares the spline-based growth estimates with linear slopes. The final inferential model evaluates treatment, stocking rate, and their interaction while accounting for year as a random effect.

Smooth splines provide a flexible description of nonlinear body-weight change without requiring a preselected polynomial shape. In this section, a separate spline is fitted to each steer using the cleaned one-record-per-animal-per-day dataset `BW_daily_spline`. The original `BW_daily` dataset is retained unchanged. The default smoothing parameter is selected by generalized cross-validation (GCV) through `stats::smooth.spline()`.

The fitted value represents smoothed body weight in kilograms. The first derivative of the spline is interpreted as the instantaneous smoothed rate of body-weight change in kilograms per day. The second derivative describes change in that daily growth rate. Derivative estimates are less stable near the beginning and end of a time series, so peak and minimum daily-gain summaries exclude a five-day boundary region.

These results are descriptive. Averaging fitted animal curves does not change the experimental unit: pasture remains the appropriate experimental unit for treatment and stocking-rate inference.

### 4.1 Fit a Smooth Spline to Each Steer

Before fitting the smooth splines, animal-days with body weight below 226.80 kg or above 544.31 kg are removed from the spline-analysis dataset. These limits are the kilogram equivalents of the original 500–1,200 lb criterion. The original `BW_daily` object remains unchanged.

```{r bw-remove-bw-outside-226-544-kg}
# Kilogram equivalents of the original source-unit screening limits.
minimum_spline_bw_kg <- 500 * pounds_to_kilograms
maximum_spline_bw_kg <- 1200 * pounds_to_kilograms

# Retain a record of observations excluded by the absolute BW limits.
bw_outside_spline_limits <- BW_daily_spline %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(BW),
    BW < minimum_spline_bw_kg | BW > maximum_spline_bw_kg
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Removal_reason = case_when(
      BW < minimum_spline_bw_kg ~ "BW below 226.80 kg",
      BW > maximum_spline_bw_kg ~ "BW above 544.31 kg",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SR, TRT, SEID, Date)

# Delete those animal-days before fitting the smooth splines.
BW_daily_spline <- BW_daily_spline %>%
  filter(
    is.na(BW) |
      between(BW, minimum_spline_bw_kg, maximum_spline_bw_kg)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Date)

cat(
  "Animal-days removed for BW below 226.80 kg or above 544.31 kg:",
  nrow(bw_outside_spline_limits), "\n"
)

bw_outside_spline_limits %>%
  count(Year, SR, TRT, Removal_reason, name = "Observations_removed") %>%
  arrange(Year, SR, TRT, Removal_reason)
```

```{r bw-spline-fit-functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# User-adjustable spline settings.
spline_min_unique_days <- 20L
spline_boundary_buffer <- 5L

# Keep this as NULL to let smooth.spline select smoothing by GCV.
# A fixed value between approximately 0 and 1 can be supplied for sensitivity analysis.
spline_spar <- NULL

# Fit one smooth spline safely.
fit_one_bw_spline <- function(dat,
                              min_unique_days = spline_min_unique_days,
                              spar = spline_spar) {
  dat <- dat %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(Day_of_Study),
      is.finite(BW)
    ) %>%
    arrange(Day_of_Study)

  if (n_distinct(dat$Day_of_Study) < min_unique_days) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  if (sd(dat$BW, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  tryCatch(
    {
      if (is.null(spar)) {
        stats::smooth.spline(
          x = dat$Day_of_Study,
          y = dat$BW,
          cv = FALSE,
          all.knots = TRUE
        )
      } else {
        stats::smooth.spline(
          x = dat$Day_of_Study,
          y = dat$BW,
          spar = spar,
          all.knots = TRUE
        )
      }
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
}

# Predict fitted BW and its first two derivatives for every day in the
# pre-defined analysis window. Previously this sequence stopped at each
# animal's last observed weighing day. Consequently, an entire pasture-period
# became NA when none of its animals had an observation exactly on the period
# end date (Pasture 5, Period 5, 2024 was the observed case).
predict_one_bw_spline <- function(model, dat, expected_days) {
  first_observed_day <- min(dat$Day_of_Study, na.rm = TRUE)
  last_observed_day <- max(dat$Day_of_Study, na.rm = TRUE)

  prediction_days <- seq.int(
    from = 1L,
    to = as.integer(expected_days),
    by = 1L
  )

  fitted_bw <- predict(model, x = prediction_days, deriv = 0)$y
  first_derivative <- predict(model, x = prediction_days, deriv = 1)$y
  second_derivative <- predict(model, x = prediction_days, deriv = 2)$y

  tibble(
    Day_of_Study = as.integer(prediction_days),
    Fitted_BW = as.numeric(fitted_bw),
    Spline_ADG = as.numeric(first_derivative),
    Spline_Acceleration = as.numeric(second_derivative),
    First_Observed_Day = as.integer(first_observed_day),
    Last_Observed_Day = as.integer(last_observed_day),
    Prediction_Extrapolated =
      Day_of_Study < First_Observed_Day |
      Day_of_Study > Last_Observed_Day
  )
}
```

```{r bw-spline-fit-by-animal, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
animal_spline_models <- BW_daily_spline %>%
  group_by(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    Start_Date, End_Date, Expected_Days
  ) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  mutate(
    N_Observations = map_int(data, nrow),
    Unique_Days = map_int(data, ~ n_distinct(.x$Day_of_Study)),
    Spline_Model = map(
      data,
      ~ fit_one_bw_spline(
        .x,
        min_unique_days = spline_min_unique_days,
        spar = spline_spar
      )
    ),
    Model_OK = map_lgl(Spline_Model, ~ !is.null(.x)),
    Spline_DF = map_dbl(
      Spline_Model,
      ~ if (is.null(.x) || length(.x$df) == 0) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        as.numeric(.x$df)
      }
    ),
    Smoothing_Parameter = map_dbl(
      Spline_Model,
      ~ if (is.null(.x) || length(.x$spar) == 0) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        as.numeric(.x$spar)
      }
    ),
    GCV_Criterion = map_dbl(
      Spline_Model,
      ~ if (is.null(.x) || length(.x$cv.crit) == 0) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        as.numeric(.x$cv.crit)
      }
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

spline_model_diagnostics <- animal_spline_models %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    N_Observations, Unique_Days, Model_OK,
    Spline_DF, Smoothing_Parameter, GCV_Criterion
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Pasture, SEID)

cat("Number of steer-year spline models attempted:",
    nrow(spline_model_diagnostics), "\n")
cat("Number fitted successfully:",
    sum(spline_model_diagnostics$Model_OK), "\n")
cat("Number not fitted:",
    sum(!spline_model_diagnostics$Model_OK), "\n")

spline_model_diagnostics %>%
  count(Year, Model_OK, name = "Animals")

# Animals without a fitted model should be reviewed for insufficient coverage
# or nonvarying BW records.
spline_model_diagnostics %>%
  filter(!Model_OK)
```

### 4.2 Generate Daily Spline Predictions and Derivatives

```{r bw-spline-predictions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
animal_spline_predictions <- animal_spline_models %>%
  filter(Model_OK) %>%
  mutate(
    Predictions = pmap(
      list(
        Spline_Model,
        data,
        Expected_Days
      ),
      predict_one_bw_spline
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    Start_Date, End_Date, Expected_Days,
    N_Observations, Unique_Days,
    Spline_DF, Smoothing_Parameter, GCV_Criterion,
    Predictions
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(Predictions) %>%
  mutate(
    Date = Start_Date + (Day_of_Study - 1L),
    Animal_ID = interaction(Year, SEID, drop = TRUE, sep = "-")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, SEID, Day_of_Study)

head(animal_spline_predictions)

# Audit how much prediction extends beyond the observed weighing range. This
# is especially important at period boundaries because period gain requires a
# fitted value on both the exact start and end dates.
spline_extrapolation_audit <- animal_spline_predictions %>%
  group_by(Year, Pasture, SEID) %>%
  summarise(
    First_Observed_Date = first(Start_Date) +
      first(First_Observed_Day) - 1L,
    Last_Observed_Date = first(Start_Date) +
      first(Last_Observed_Day) - 1L,
    Extrapolated_Days = sum(Prediction_Extrapolated),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Pasture, SEID)

spline_extrapolation_audit %>%
  group_by(Year, Pasture) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n(),
    Last_Observed_Date = max(Last_Observed_Date),
    Animals_With_Extrapolation = sum(Extrapolated_Days > 0L),
    Maximum_Extrapolated_Days = max(Extrapolated_Days),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### 4.3 Descriptive Mean Spline Curves

The summaries below average the independently fitted steer curves at each study day. The ribbons describe variation among steer fitted values and are not pasture-level inferential confidence intervals.

#### 4.3.1 Treatment Curves Within Stocking Rate and Year

```{r bw-spline-trt-summary, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
spline_trt_summary <- animal_spline_predictions %>%
  group_by(Year, Day_of_Study, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Mean_Fitted_BW = mean(Fitted_BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Fitted_BW = sd(Fitted_BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_Fitted_BW = if_else(
      Animals > 1,
      SD_Fitted_BW / sqrt(Animals),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Lower_95 = Mean_Fitted_BW - 1.96 * SE_Fitted_BW,
    Upper_95 = Mean_Fitted_BW + 1.96 * SE_Fitted_BW,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  spline_trt_summary,
  aes(
    x = Day_of_Study,
    y = Mean_Fitted_BW,
    color = TRT,
    fill = TRT,
    group = TRT
  )
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Lower_95, ymax = Upper_95),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(Year ~ SR, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Smooth-Spline Body Weight by Treatment and Stocking Rate",
    subtitle = "Ribbon is the descriptive 95% interval around the mean fitted animal curve",
    x = "Day of study",
    y = "Mean fitted body weight (kg)",
    color = "Treatment",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### 4.4 Smooth Daily Gain from the First Derivative

`Spline_ADG` is the first derivative of the fitted body-weight curve. Positive values indicate increasing fitted BW and negative values indicate decreasing fitted BW at that point in the grazing period. Because daily Smart Scale measurements may be noisy, the derivative should be interpreted as a smoothed trend rather than an observed one-day gain.

```{r bw-spline-adg-summary, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
spline_adg_summary <- animal_spline_predictions %>%
  group_by(Year, Day_of_Study, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Mean_Spline_ADG = mean(Spline_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Spline_ADG = sd(Spline_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE_Spline_ADG = if_else(
      Animals > 1,
      SD_Spline_ADG / sqrt(Animals),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Lower_95 = Mean_Spline_ADG - 1.96 * SE_Spline_ADG,
    Upper_95 = Mean_Spline_ADG + 1.96 * SE_Spline_ADG,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  spline_adg_summary,
  aes(
    x = Day_of_Study,
    y = Mean_Spline_ADG,
    color = TRT,
    fill = TRT,
    group = TRT
  )
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Lower_95, ymax = Upper_95),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(Year ~ SR, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Smooth Daily Body-Weight Change",
    subtitle = "First derivative of the individual steer smooth splines",
    x = "Day of study",
    y = "Smoothed daily change (kg/day)",
    color = "Treatment",
    fill = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### 4.5 Animal-Level Spline Growth Metrics

The period-average spline ADG is calculated from the difference between fitted end and fitted start BW divided by the fitted study span. Mean, peak, and minimum derivative summaries use only interior days after removing the boundary buffer specified above.

```{r bw-spline-growth-metric-functions}
safe_finite_mean <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else mean(x)
}

safe_finite_max <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else max(x)
}

safe_finite_min <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else min(x)
}

safe_finite_cor <- function(x, y) {
  keep <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  if (sum(keep) < 3) NA_real_ else cor(x[keep], y[keep])
}

safe_extreme_day <- function(values, days, direction = c("max", "min")) {
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  keep <- is.finite(values) & is.finite(days)

  if (!any(keep)) {
    return(NA_integer_)
  }

  values <- values[keep]
  days <- days[keep]

  if (direction == "max") {
    as.integer(days[which.max(values)])
  } else {
    as.integer(days[which.min(values)])
  }
}
```

```{r bw-spline-animal-growth-metrics}
animal_spline_metrics <- animal_spline_predictions %>%
  group_by(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    Unique_Days, Spline_DF,
    Smoothing_Parameter, GCV_Criterion
  ) %>%
  arrange(Day_of_Study, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    First_Predicted_Day = min(Day_of_Study),
    Last_Predicted_Day = max(Day_of_Study),
    Interior_Day =
      Day_of_Study >= First_Predicted_Day + spline_boundary_buffer &
      Day_of_Study <= Last_Predicted_Day - spline_boundary_buffer
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    First_Day = first(Day_of_Study),
    Last_Day = last(Day_of_Study),
    Fitted_Start_BW = first(Fitted_BW),
    Fitted_End_BW = last(Fitted_BW),
    Smooth_BW_Change = Fitted_End_BW - Fitted_Start_BW,
    Smooth_Period_ADG = if_else(
      Last_Day > First_Day,
      Smooth_BW_Change / (Last_Day - First_Day),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Mean_Interior_ADG = safe_finite_mean(Spline_ADG[Interior_Day]),
    Peak_Interior_ADG = safe_finite_max(Spline_ADG[Interior_Day]),
    Peak_ADG_Day = safe_extreme_day(
      Spline_ADG[Interior_Day],
      Day_of_Study[Interior_Day],
      direction = "max"
    ),
    Minimum_Interior_ADG = safe_finite_min(Spline_ADG[Interior_Day]),
    Minimum_ADG_Day = safe_extreme_day(
      Spline_ADG[Interior_Day],
      Day_of_Study[Interior_Day],
      direction = "min"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Pasture, SEID)

animal_spline_metrics
```

```{r bw-spline-growth-group-summary}
spline_growth_summary <- animal_spline_metrics %>%
  group_by(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n(),

    Mean_Fitted_End_BW = mean(Fitted_End_BW, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Smooth_BW_Change = mean(Smooth_BW_Change, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Smooth_Period_ADG = mean(Smooth_Period_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_Smooth_Period_ADG = sd(Smooth_Period_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Smooth_Period_ADG = median(Smooth_Period_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Peak_Interior_ADG = mean(Peak_Interior_ADG, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Peak_ADG_Day = mean(Peak_ADG_Day, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, TRT, SR, Pasture)
```

### 4.6 Spline Residual Diagnostics

Residuals quantify the difference between observed daily BW and the corresponding fitted spline value. Large residuals may indicate temporary scale variation, unusual animal behavior at the scale, or records requiring source-data review.

```{r bw-spline-residual-diagnostics}
spline_observed_fit <- BW_daily %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    Date, Day_of_Study, BW, BW_Source
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    animal_spline_predictions %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Year, SEID, Day_of_Study,
        Fitted_BW, Spline_ADG, Spline_Acceleration
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Day_of_Study")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Spline_Residual = BW - Fitted_BW,
    Absolute_Residual = abs(Spline_Residual)
  )

spline_residual_summary <- spline_observed_fit %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals = n_distinct(SEID),
    Observations = n(),
    Mean_Residual = mean(Spline_Residual, na.rm = TRUE),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(Spline_Residual^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    MAE = mean(Absolute_Residual, na.rm = TRUE),
    Residual_SD = sd(Spline_Residual, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

spline_residual_summary
```

### 4.7 Compare Spline ADG with the Earlier Linear Growth Slope

The linear regression slope summarizes the entire period with one straight line. The spline period-average ADG also summarizes the entire period, but its underlying curve can represent nonlinear growth. Agreement between these two measures is a useful diagnostic; large disagreements identify animals whose trajectories are strongly nonlinear or affected by endpoints.

```{r bw-spline-linear-comparison}
spline_linear_comparison <- animal_spline_metrics %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
    Smooth_Period_ADG
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    animal_growth %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Year, SEID, Tag, Pasture, TRT, SR,
        Regression_ADG, Endpoint_ADG
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Tag", "Pasture", "TRT", "SR")
  )

spline_linear_agreement <- spline_linear_comparison %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Complete_Pairs = sum(
      complete.cases(Smooth_Period_ADG, Regression_ADG)
    ),
    Correlation = safe_finite_cor(
      Smooth_Period_ADG,
      Regression_ADG
    ),
    Mean_Difference = mean(
      Smooth_Period_ADG - Regression_ADG,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

spline_linear_agreement
```

### 4.8 Mixed-Effects Model and ANOVA

#### 4.8.1 Fit the Mixed-Effects Model

```{r bw-mixed-effects-model}

# Smooth_Period_ADG is one whole-interval spline ADG value per animal-year in
# animal_spline_metrics. It is NOT a repeated-period response.
adg_model_data <- animal_spline_metrics %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(Smooth_Period_ADG),
    !is.na(TRT),
    !is.na(SR),
    !is.na(Year),
    !is.na(Pasture),
    !is.na(SEID)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    TRT = as.character(TRT),
    SR = as.character(SR),

    TRT = factor(
      TRT,
      levels = c("Continuous", "Rotational")
    ),

    SR = factor(
      SR,
      levels = c("Light", "Moderate", "Heavy")
    ),

    Year = factor(Year),
    Pasture = factor(Pasture),
    SEID = factor(SEID)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

# Verify all retained source labels remain valid after factor conversion.
if (anyNA(adg_model_data[c("TRT", "SR", "Year", "Pasture", "SEID")])) {
  stop("Unexpected TRT/SR labels in animal_spline_metrics; review assignment before fitting.")
}
# Verify treatment structure
table(adg_model_data$TRT, adg_model_data$SR)
table(adg_model_data$Year)
nrow(adg_model_data)

# Enforce one whole-interval spline ADG per animal-year
if (anyDuplicated(adg_model_data[c("Year", "SEID")])) {
  stop(
    "animal_spline_metrics contains more than one Smooth_Period_ADG row for ",
    "at least one animal-year. Resolve duplicates before fitting the ADG model."
  )
}

# Confirm all model variables are complete
model_vars <- c(
  "Smooth_Period_ADG",
  "TRT",
  "SR",
  "Year",
  "Pasture"
)

# A whole-interval response is observed once per animal-year; no animal
# intercept is estimable or needed for repetition. Preserve Year and persistent
# Pasture as in the reference implementation; neither creates pasture replication.
contrasts(adg_model_data$TRT) <- contr.sum(nlevels(adg_model_data$TRT))
contrasts(adg_model_data$SR) <- contr.sum(nlevels(adg_model_data$SR))
smooth_adg_model <- afri_fit_lmm(
  Smooth_Period_ADG ~ TRT * SR + (1 | Year) + (1 | Pasture),
  data = adg_model_data,
  question_id = "table2_adg__Smooth_Period_ADG",
  REML = TRUE
)
# Compatibility name: this is the same fit, not a refitted model.
smooth_adg_model_anova <- smooth_adg_model

summary(smooth_adg_model)
VarCorr(smooth_adg_model)
lme4::isSingular(smooth_adg_model, tol = 1e-4)

warning(
  "TRT and SR management P-values remain exploratory/conditional because ",
  "each TRT x SR combination is represented by one physical pasture."
)
```

#### 4.8.2 Type III ANOVA for Fixed Effects
```{r bw-mixed-effects-type-iii-anova}
# One inference object is reused here and in all final statistical tables.
smooth_adg_inference <- afri_inference(smooth_adg_model, emm_specs = ~ TRT * SR)
smooth_adg_anova <- smooth_adg_inference$anova
smooth_adg_anova
```

#### 4.8.3 Assess Residual Normality

```{r bw-mixed-effects-residual-normality}
smooth_adg_diagnostics <- afri_diagnose_lmm(smooth_adg_model, "table2_adg__Smooth_Period_ADG")
smooth_adg_residuals <- stats::residuals(smooth_adg_model)
# Retain the compatibility object as the already calculated numerical test table.
smooth_adg_shapiro <- smooth_adg_diagnostics$summary %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, n, shapiro_W, shapiro_p, shapiro_status)
smooth_adg_shapiro
smooth_adg_variance_review <- smooth_adg_diagnostics$variance_review
smooth_adg_variance_review
for (diagnostic_plot in smooth_adg_diagnostics$plots) print(diagnostic_plot)
# A significant Shapiro-Wilk result alone does not warrant changing this model.
```

#### 4.8.4 Compute Tukey-Adjusted Comparisons
```{r bw-mixed-effects-tukey-comparisons}
smooth_adg_emmeans <- smooth_adg_inference$emm
smooth_adg_inference$emmeans
# Reorganize the retained grid rather than recomputing EMMs from the model.
tukey_trt_within_sr <- emmeans::contrast(smooth_adg_emmeans, method = "pairwise", by = "SR", adjust = "tukey")
tukey_sr_within_trt <- emmeans::contrast(smooth_adg_emmeans, method = "pairwise", by = "TRT", adjust = "tukey")
tukey_trt_within_sr
tukey_sr_within_trt
```

### 4.9 Smooth-Spline and Inferential Outputs to Retain

The principal spline-analysis objects are:

- `animal_spline_models`: one fitted spline object per steer-year, including model diagnostics;
- `animal_spline_predictions`: fitted BW, first derivative, and second derivative for each steer and study day;
- `spline_trt_summary`: descriptive mean fitted curves by year, treatment, and stocking rate;
- `spline_pasture_summary`: pasture-level mean fitted body-weight curves;
- `spline_adg_summary` and `spline_pasture_adg`: smooth daily-gain summaries;
- `animal_spline_metrics`: steer-level fitted start BW, fitted end BW, smooth period ADG, and interior derivative metrics;
- `spline_growth_summary`: pasture-specific summaries of animal spline metrics;
- `spline_observed_fit`: observed BW, fitted BW, derivatives, and residuals;
- `largest_spline_residuals`: the 50 observations with the largest absolute spline residuals;
- `spline_linear_comparison`: comparison of spline-based and linear animal growth summaries;
- `smooth_adg_model_anova` and `smooth_adg_anova`: the mixed-effects model and Type III fixed-effect tests;
- `smooth_adg_emmeans`, `tukey_trt_within_sr`, and `tukey_sr_within_trt`: estimated marginal means and Tukey-adjusted comparisons.

For formal statistical inference, `Smooth_Period_ADG` is analyzed as one animal-level whole-interval response per animal-year. Different steers were used each year. The model recognizes pasture as the treatment-level experimental unit and includes random intercepts for Year and persistent physical Pasture; Pasture_Year is not fitted as a random intercept. Daily spline predictions or derivatives are not analyzed as independent treatment replicates. Because only three years were observed, the Year variance component should be interpreted cautiously.

## 5. Spatial Production Efficiency: Gain per Area Grazed

This section evaluates steer body-weight production from a land-use perspective. The principal response is the **gain-to-area-grazed ratio**, calculated as estimated total liveweight gain in kilograms divided by the area available to the animals in hectares during each documented grazing period.

Two complementary measures are reported:

1. **Animal performance:** mean period gain and mean period ADG per steer.
2. **Land productivity:** estimated total pasture gain per active hectare, which combines animal performance, animal numbers, period length, and area grazed.

For all six pastures, the active-area denominator is the HMM-derived,
GPS-observed grazed area for the corresponding year, pasture, and rotation
period. The period definition and rotational-subdivision assignment stay
unchanged. Whole-pasture and scheduled-rotation polygon areas are retained only
for boundary definition, quality control, and contextual maps. Period-level
results are descriptive because treatment and stocking rate are applied at the
pasture level, and the study has one pasture for each treatment-by-stocking-rate
combination within a year.


### 5.1 Spatial Packages, File Locations, and Reported Pasture Areas

The geometry-only reader in this section is intentionally independent of `.dbf`, `.shx`, and `.prj` files. It sequentially reads polygon geometry from each `.shp` file, reconstructs the spatial features, and then applies explicit coordinate-reference-system assumptions. The complete shapefile sidecars should still be retained and supplied when available because they contain attributes, an index, and authoritative projection metadata.

```{r bw-spatial-production-settings, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
required_spatial_packages <- c("sf")
missing_spatial_packages <- required_spatial_packages[
  !vapply(required_spatial_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_spatial_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following packages before running the spatial section: ",
    paste(missing_spatial_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Folder containing CTWD_Pastures.shp and the P*_R*.shp files.
# Change this path if the GIS files are stored elsewhere.
gis_data_dir <- resolve_project_path(params$gis_data_dir)

ranch_shapefile <- file.path(gis_data_dir, "CTWD_Pastures.shp")
rotation_shapefiles <- list.files(
  path = gis_data_dir,
  pattern = "^P[234]_R[1-4].*\\.shp$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

if (!file.exists(ranch_shapefile)) {
  stop("CTWD_Pastures.shp was not found in gis_data_dir.")
}

if (length(rotation_shapefiles) == 0) {
  stop("No P2/P3/P4 rotation shapefiles were found in gis_data_dir.")
}

# Coordinate-system assumptions based on the coordinates stored in the supplied files.
# CTWD_Pastures: projected UTM coordinates near easting 270,000 and northing 4,870,000.
# Rotation files: longitude/latitude coordinates near -101.85, 43.94.
ranch_source_crs <- 32614       # WGS 84 / UTM zone 14N
rotation_source_crs <- 4326     # WGS 84 longitude/latitude
spatial_analysis_crs <- 32614   # Equal-distance/area work in metres

square_metres_per_hectare <- 10000
bw_unit_label <- "kg"

pasture_area_reference <- tibble(
  Pasture_ID = 1:6,
  Supplied_Pasture_Hectares =
    c(73.4, 127.4, 161.7, 78.1, 129.2, 179.3) * acres_to_hectares,
  Grazing_System = c(
    "Continuous", "Rotational", "Rotational",
    "Rotational", "Continuous", "Continuous"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Pasture_Label = paste("Pasture", Pasture_ID))

pasture_area_reference
```

#### 5.1.1 Audit Shapefile Components

This audit documents which sidecar files are available. Missing sidecars do not prevent the geometry-only reader from running, but the final analysis should be rerun with the complete GIS datasets when possible.

```{r bw-shapefile-component-audit}
all_shp_paths <- c(ranch_shapefile, rotation_shapefiles)

shapefile_component_audit <- map_dfr(all_shp_paths, function(shp_path) {
  stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(shp_path)
  tibble(
    Layer = basename(stem),
    SHP = file.exists(paste0(stem, ".shp")),
    SHX = file.exists(paste0(stem, ".shx")),
    DBF = file.exists(paste0(stem, ".dbf")),
    PRJ = file.exists(paste0(stem, ".prj"))
  )
})

shapefile_component_audit
```

### 5.2 Read Polygon Geometry Without the Missing Sidecar Files

Reuse the already read polygon shapefiles from the HMM/GPS section after confirming that files, projection assumptions, pasture mapping, and rotation keys match. The preceding geometry-only reader handles Polygon, PolygonZ, and PolygonM; it cannot reconstruct unavailable `.dbf` attributes.

```{r bw-geometry-only-shapefile-reader, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# The HMM/GPS section already read these files, used these CRS assumptions,
# corrected the P1/P2 overlap, and clipped the same rotational subdivisions.
# Runtime equivalence checks prevent reuse when source settings differ.
if (!identical(normalizePath(ranch_shapefile, mustWork = TRUE),
               normalizePath(bw_spatial_cache$ranch_shapefile, mustWork = TRUE)) ||
    !identical(sort(normalizePath(rotation_shapefiles, mustWork = TRUE)),
               sort(normalizePath(bw_spatial_cache$rotation_shapefiles, mustWork = TRUE))) ||
    !identical(c(ranch_source_crs, rotation_source_crs, spatial_analysis_crs),
               c(bw_spatial_cache$ranch_source_crs, bw_spatial_cache$rotation_source_crs,
                 bw_spatial_cache$spatial_analysis_crs))) {
  stop("BW and HMM spatial source files or CRS assumptions differ; do not merge unequal geometry.")
}
ranch_raw_sf <- bw_spatial_cache$ranch_raw_sf
rotation_metadata <- bw_spatial_cache$rotation_metadata
# Reassemble raw layer attributes from the in-memory geometry list. Raw polygons
# are needed uniquely for the BW overlap audit; no shapefiles are read again.
rotation_raw_sf <- do.call(rbind, bw_spatial_cache$rotation_raw_list) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(rotation_metadata %>%
    dplyr::select(Rotation_Key, Pasture_ID, Rotation_Number, File), by = "Rotation_Key") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Pasture_ID, Rotation_Number)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rotation_raw_sf$Rotation_Key))
sf::st_bbox(ranch_raw_sf)
sf::st_bbox(rotation_raw_sf)
```

### 5.3 Identify Summer Pastures 1–6 and Validate Their Areas

Because the CTWD pasture attribute table was not supplied, Pastures 1–6 are identified from the polygon-record order in the provided geometry. Pastures 2–4 were independently verified by maximum spatial overlap with the P2, P3, and P4 rotation polygons. Pastures 1, 5, and 6 were identified from the remaining adjacent summer-pasture polygons and their close agreement with the supplied area in hectares.

The mapping is:

- Pasture 1 → CTWD record 9
- Pasture 2 → CTWD record 8
- Pasture 3 → CTWD record 10
- Pasture 4 → CTWD record 13
- Pasture 5 → CTWD record 12
- Pasture 6 → CTWD record 11

This mapping should be replaced with an attribute-based selection when the `.dbf` file becomes available.

```{r bw-pasture-identification-and-validation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
pasture_feature_map <- tibble(
  Pasture_ID = 1:6,
  Ranch_Feature_ID = c(9L, 8L, 10L, 13L, 12L, 11L)
)

if (!identical(as.data.frame(pasture_feature_map),
               as.data.frame(bw_spatial_cache$pasture_feature_map))) {
  stop("BW and HMM pasture-to-CTWD-record mappings differ.")
}
pasture_sf <- bw_spatial_cache$pasture_sf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pasture_area_reference, by = "Pasture_ID") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Pasture_ID) %>%
  mutate(
    GIS_Pasture_Hectares = as.numeric(sf::st_area(geometry)) /
      square_metres_per_hectare,
    Hectare_Difference = GIS_Pasture_Hectares - Supplied_Pasture_Hectares,
    Hectare_Difference_Percent = 100 * Hectare_Difference /
      Supplied_Pasture_Hectares
  )

if (nrow(pasture_sf) != 6L) {
  stop("The CTWD record mapping did not return all six summer pastures.")
}

pasture_area_validation <- pasture_sf %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Pasture_ID, Ranch_Feature_ID, Grazing_System,
    Supplied_Pasture_Hectares, GIS_Pasture_Hectares,
    Hectare_Difference, Hectare_Difference_Percent
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

pasture_area_validation

if (any(abs(pasture_sf$Hectare_Difference_Percent) > 10)) {
  warning(
    "At least one GIS pasture area differs from the supplied area in hectares by more than 10%. ",
    "Verify the pasture mapping and CRS before interpreting gain per hectare."
  )
}
```

#### 5.3.1 Verify Rotational-Pasture Overlap

```{r bw-rotational-overlap-validation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rotation_group_union <- rotation_raw_sf %>%
  group_by(Pasture_ID) %>%
  summarise(geometry = sf::st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop")

rotation_pasture_overlap <- sf::st_intersection(
  rotation_group_union,
  pasture_sf %>% dplyr::select(Pasture_ID_CTWD = Pasture_ID)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Overlap_Hectares = as.numeric(sf::st_area(geometry)) /
      square_metres_per_hectare
  ) %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(Pasture_ID) %>%
  slice_max(Overlap_Hectares, n = 1L, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Expected_Match = Pasture_ID == Pasture_ID_CTWD,
    Overlap_Hectares = round(Overlap_Hectares, 2)
  )

rotation_pasture_overlap

if (any(!rotation_pasture_overlap$Expected_Match)) {
  warning("At least one rotational pasture did not match its expected CTWD polygon.")
}
```

### 5.4 Prepare and Validate Rotation Polygons

Each rotation polygon is clipped to its corresponding whole-pasture polygon. Its raw GIS area in hectares is then adjusted by the ratio of supplied whole-pasture area in hectares to GIS whole-pasture area in hectares. This preserves the relative size of each rotation polygon while using the producer-supplied pasture area in hectares as the authoritative whole-pasture denominator.

```{r bw-rotation-polygon-preparation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Reuse the identical HMM clipped boundaries; enrich only the new BW area audit.
if (!setequal(bw_spatial_cache$rotation_sf$Rotation_Key, rotation_metadata$Rotation_Key) ||
    anyDuplicated(bw_spatial_cache$rotation_sf$Rotation_Key) ||
    !isTRUE(sf::st_crs(bw_spatial_cache$rotation_sf) == sf::st_crs(pasture_sf))) {
  stop("HMM clipped rotation geometry does not match BW rotation keys/CRS.")
}
rotation_sf <- bw_spatial_cache$rotation_sf %>%
  dplyr::left_join(rotation_metadata %>%
    dplyr::select(Rotation_Key, Source_File = File), by = "Rotation_Key") %>%
  left_join(
    pasture_sf %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Pasture_ID, Supplied_Pasture_Hectares,
        GIS_Pasture_Hectares
      ),
    by = "Pasture_ID"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    GIS_Active_Hectares = as.numeric(sf::st_area(geometry)) /
      square_metres_per_hectare,
    Area_Scaling_Factor = Supplied_Pasture_Hectares /
      GIS_Pasture_Hectares,
    Adjusted_Active_Hectares = GIS_Active_Hectares * Area_Scaling_Factor,
    Active_Percent_of_Pasture = 100 * Adjusted_Active_Hectares /
      Supplied_Pasture_Hectares
  ) %>%
  arrange(Pasture_ID, Rotation_Number)

rotation_area_validation <- rotation_sf %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Pasture_ID, Rotation_Number, Rotation_Key, Source_File,
    GIS_Active_Hectares, Adjusted_Active_Hectares,
    Supplied_Pasture_Hectares, Active_Percent_of_Pasture
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

rotation_area_validation
```

### 5.5 Rotation Schedule for 2023–2025

The schedule below reproduces the supplied rotation dates. Scheduled periods are intersected with the body-weight analysis windows. Therefore, the final 2023 and 2024 periods are truncated at the analysis end dates, and dates without a documented rotation assignment are explicitly reported rather than silently assigned.

```{r bw-rotation-schedule, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# The source dates and rotation assignments were checked against the original
# BW schedule. Verify those exact values before reusing the HMM schedule.
rotation_schedule <- behavior_rotation_schedule %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Year = as.integer(as.character(Year)),
    Period_ID = as.integer(Rotation_Period), Scheduled_Start = Rotation_Start,
    Scheduled_End = Rotation_End, P2_Rotation, P3_Rotation, P4_Rotation,
    Period_Label = paste0("RGP", Rotation_Period)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Year, Period_ID)
bw_expected_schedule_rows <- c(
  "2023|1|2023-06-19|2023-07-03|1|1|1",
  "2023|2|2023-07-04|2023-07-17|2|2|2",
  "2023|3|2023-07-18|2023-07-31|3|3|3",
  "2023|4|2023-08-01|2023-08-14|4|4|1",
  "2023|5|2023-08-15|2023-08-28|1|1|2",
  "2024|1|2024-06-13|2024-06-27|4|4|3",
  "2024|2|2024-06-28|2024-07-11|3|3|2",
  "2024|3|2024-07-12|2024-07-26|2|2|1",
  "2024|4|2024-07-27|2024-08-10|1|1|3",
  "2024|5|2024-08-11|2024-08-25|4|4|2",
  "2025|1|2025-06-12|2025-06-25|1|1|1",
  "2025|2|2025-06-26|2025-07-09|2|2|2",
  "2025|3|2025-07-10|2025-07-23|3|3|3",
  "2025|4|2025-07-24|2025-08-06|4|4|1",
  "2025|5|2025-08-07|2025-08-20|1|1|2"
)
bw_observed_schedule_rows <- apply(as.data.frame(rotation_schedule[,
  c("Year", "Period_ID", "Scheduled_Start", "Scheduled_End",
    "P2_Rotation", "P3_Rotation", "P4_Rotation")]), 1L, paste, collapse = "|")
if (!identical(unname(bw_observed_schedule_rows), bw_expected_schedule_rows)) {
  stop("HMM rotation schedule differs from the documented BW schedule.")
}

analysis_windows_numeric <- analysis_windows %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(as.character(Year)))

period_table <- rotation_schedule %>%
  inner_join(analysis_windows_numeric, by = "Year") %>%
  mutate(
    Analysis_Start = pmax(Scheduled_Start, Start_Date),
    Analysis_End = pmin(Scheduled_End, End_Date),
    Period_Days = as.integer(Analysis_End - Analysis_Start) + 1L,
    Gain_Interval_Days = as.integer(Analysis_End - Analysis_Start),
    Period_Midpoint = Analysis_Start + floor((Period_Days - 1L) / 2L),
    Truncated_to_BW_Window = Analysis_Start != Scheduled_Start |
      Analysis_End != Scheduled_End
  ) %>%
  filter(Analysis_Start <= Analysis_End) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, Period_ID, Period_Label,
    Scheduled_Start, Scheduled_End,
    Analysis_Start, Analysis_End,
    Period_Days, Gain_Interval_Days, Period_Midpoint,
    Truncated_to_BW_Window,
    P2_Rotation, P3_Rotation, P4_Rotation
  )

period_table
```

#### 5.5.1 Expand the Schedule to All Six Pastures and Assign Active Area

```{r bw-pasture-period-active-area, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
period_pasture_schedule <- period_table %>%
  tidyr::crossing(Pasture_ID = 1:6) %>%
  left_join(pasture_area_reference, by = "Pasture_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    Rotation_Number = case_when(
      Pasture_ID == 2L ~ P2_Rotation,
      Pasture_ID == 3L ~ P3_Rotation,
      Pasture_ID == 4L ~ P4_Rotation,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    ),
    Rotation_Key = if_else(
      Grazing_System == "Rotational",
      paste0("P", Pasture_ID, "_R", Rotation_Number),
      NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    gps_active_area_lookup,
    by = c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID",
      "Period_ID" = "Rotation_Period"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    HMM_Area_Window_Matches_Schedule =
      Scheduled_Start == HMM_Area_Start &
      Scheduled_End == HMM_Area_End,
    Schedule_Label = if_else(
      Grazing_System == "Continuous",
      "Whole-pasture boundary",
      paste0("R", Rotation_Number)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID)

if (anyNA(period_pasture_schedule$HMM_Area_Window_Matches_Schedule) ||
    !all(period_pasture_schedule$HMM_Area_Window_Matches_Schedule)) {
  stop("HMM active-area windows do not match the BW scheduled periods.")
}
# Truncated_to_BW_Window records that an endpoint gain can cover fewer dates
# than the complete scheduled HMM area window; retain that interpretation audit.

if (any(!is.finite(period_pasture_schedule$Active_Hectares) |
        period_pasture_schedule$Active_Hectares <= 0)) {
  stop("At least one pasture-period does not have a valid active area in hectares.")
}

period_pasture_schedule %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, Period_ID, Analysis_Start, Analysis_End,
    Pasture_ID, Grazing_System, Schedule_Label,
    HMM_Area_Start, HMM_Area_End,
    Active_Hectares, Available_Hectares, Active_Area_Percent,
    Active_Grid_Cells, Grazing_GPS_Points, Active_Area_Source
  ) %>%
  mutate(Active_Hectares = round(Active_Hectares, 2))
```

```{r bw-schedule-coverage-audit}
analysis_calendar <- analysis_windows_numeric %>%
  mutate(Date = map2(Start_Date, End_Date, ~ seq.Date(.x, .y, by = "day"))) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, Date) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(Date)

covered_rotation_dates <- period_table %>%
  mutate(
    Date = map2(
      Analysis_Start,
      Analysis_End,
      ~ seq.Date(.x, .y, by = "day")
    )

  dplyr::select(Year, Period_ID, Date) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(Date)

  anti_join(covered_rotation_dates, by = c("Year", "Date")) %>%
  arrange(Year, Date)

schedule_coverage_summary <- analysis_calendar %>%

  left_join(

    Rotation_Coverage_Percent = round(
```

### 5.6 Estimate Animal and Pasture Gain Within Each Period

Period gain is calculated from the steer-specific smooth spline:

\[
\text{Period gain}_{i} = \widehat{BW}_{i,\,end} - \widehat{BW}_{i,\,start}
\]

The pasture total is standardized to all animals assigned to that pasture-year:

\[
\widehat{G}_{pasture,period} = \overline{G}_{complete\ animals} \times N_{assigned}
\]

This standardization prevents a pasture with one missing boundary prediction from appearing to have lower total gain solely because fewer animals contributed. The completeness percentage and unstandardized complete-animal total are retained for transparency.

```{r bw-spline-period-animal-gain, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
safe_mean_finite <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0L) NA_real_ else mean(x)
}

safe_sd_finite <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 2L) NA_real_ else stats::sd(x)
}

safe_sum_finite <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0L) NA_real_ else sum(x)
}

spline_predictions_production <- animal_spline_predictions %>%
  transmute(
    Year = as.integer(as.character(Year)),
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    Fitted_BW,
    Spline_ADG,
    Prediction_Extrapolated
  )

production_animal_assignments <- BW_daily %>%
  transmute(
    Year = as.integer(as.character(Year)),
    SEID = as.character(SEID),
    Tag = as.character(Tag),
    Pasture_ID = as.integer(as.character(Pasture)),
    TRT = as.character(TRT),
    SR = as.character(SR)
  ) %>%
  distinct()

animal_period_grid <- production_animal_assignments %>%
  inner_join(period_table, by = "Year")

spline_period_animal_gain <- animal_period_grid %>%
  left_join(
    spline_predictions_production %>%
      transmute(
        Year, SEID,
        Analysis_Start = Date,
        Start_Fitted_BW = Fitted_BW,
        Start_Spline_ADG = Spline_ADG,
        Start_Extrapolated = Prediction_Extrapolated
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Analysis_Start")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    spline_predictions_production %>%
      transmute(
        Year, SEID,
        Analysis_End = Date,
        End_Fitted_BW = Fitted_BW,
        End_Spline_ADG = Spline_ADG,
        End_Extrapolated = Prediction_Extrapolated
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Analysis_End")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Complete_Period_Boundaries = is.finite(Start_Fitted_BW) &
      is.finite(End_Fitted_BW),
    Boundary_Extrapolated = dplyr::coalesce(Start_Extrapolated, FALSE) |
      dplyr::coalesce(End_Extrapolated, FALSE),
    Period_Gain = if_else(
      Complete_Period_Boundaries,
      End_Fitted_BW - Start_Fitted_BW,
      NA_real_
    ),
    Period_ADG = if_else(
      Complete_Period_Boundaries & Gain_Interval_Days > 0,
      Period_Gain / Gain_Interval_Days,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID, SEID)

period_boundary_audit <- spline_period_animal_gain %>%
  group_by(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals_Assigned = n_distinct(SEID),
    Complete_Boundaries = sum(Complete_Period_Boundaries),
    Extrapolated_Boundaries = sum(
      Complete_Period_Boundaries & Boundary_Extrapolated
    ),
    Missing_Boundaries = sum(!Complete_Period_Boundaries),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID)

period_boundary_audit

if (any(period_boundary_audit$Complete_Boundaries == 0L)) {
  warning(
    "At least one pasture-period still has no complete spline boundaries; ",
    "review period_boundary_audit before interpreting production results."
  )
}
```

#### 5.6.1 Build the Pasture-Period Production Table

```{r bw-pasture-period-production-table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
production_by_pasture_period <- spline_period_animal_gain %>%
  group_by(
    Year, Period_ID, Period_Label,
    Analysis_Start, Analysis_End,
    Period_Days, Gain_Interval_Days,
    Pasture_ID, TRT, SR
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals_Assigned = n_distinct(SEID),
    Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries = sum(Complete_Period_Boundaries),
    Animals_With_Extrapolated_Boundary = sum(
      Complete_Period_Boundaries & Boundary_Extrapolated
    ),
    Mean_Animal_Period_Gain = safe_mean_finite(Period_Gain),
    SD_Animal_Period_Gain = safe_sd_finite(Period_Gain),
    Median_Animal_Period_Gain = if (
      any(is.finite(Period_Gain))
    ) median(Period_Gain, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    Mean_Period_ADG = safe_mean_finite(Period_ADG),
    Complete_Animal_Total_Gain = safe_sum_finite(Period_Gain),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Complete_Assigned_Percent = 100 *
      Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries / Animals_Assigned,
    SE_Animal_Period_Gain = if_else(
      Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries >= 2L,
      SD_Animal_Period_Gain /
        sqrt(Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Estimated_Total_Pasture_Gain = Mean_Animal_Period_Gain *
      Animals_Assigned
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    period_pasture_schedule %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID,
        Grazing_System, Supplied_Pasture_Hectares,
        Rotation_Number, Rotation_Key,
        HMM_Area_Start, HMM_Area_End,
        Active_Hectares, Available_Hectares, Active_Area_Percent,
        Grid_Size_m, Minimum_Grazing_Fixes,
        Active_Grid_Cells, Grazing_GPS_Points,
        Active_Area_Source
      ),
    by = c("Year", "Period_ID", "Pasture_ID")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Gain_per_Hectare = Estimated_Total_Pasture_Gain / Active_Hectares,
    Gain_per_Hectare_per_Day = Gain_per_Hectare / Gain_Interval_Days,
    Instantaneous_Animals_per_Hectare = Animals_Assigned / Active_Hectares,
    Animal_Days_per_Hectare = Animals_Assigned * Period_Days / Active_Hectares,
    Gain_per_Hectare_SE = SE_Animal_Period_Gain *
      Animals_Assigned / Active_Hectares,
    T_Critical_95 = if_else(
      Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries >= 2L,
      qt(0.975, df = Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries - 1L),
      NA_real_
    ),
    Gain_per_Hectare_CI_Lower = Gain_per_Hectare -
      T_Critical_95 * Gain_per_Hectare_SE,
    Gain_per_Hectare_CI_Upper = Gain_per_Hectare +
      T_Critical_95 * Gain_per_Hectare_SE
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID)

production_by_pasture_period %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year, Period_ID, Analysis_Start, Analysis_End,
    Pasture_ID, Grazing_System, TRT, SR,
    Rotation_Number, Active_Hectares,
    Animals_Assigned, Animals_With_Complete_Boundaries,
    Animals_With_Extrapolated_Boundary,
    Complete_Assigned_Percent,
    Mean_Animal_Period_Gain, Mean_Period_ADG,
    Estimated_Total_Pasture_Gain,
    Gain_per_Hectare, Gain_per_Hectare_per_Day,
    Instantaneous_Animals_per_Hectare,
    Animal_Days_per_Hectare
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

### 5.7 Production-Perspective Graphics

#### 5.7.1 Gain per Active Hectare Through the Rotation Periods

The vertical intervals represent descriptive within-pasture uncertainty propagated from variation among steer-specific period gains. They are not treatment-level confidence intervals because pasture is the experimental unit.

```{r bw-gain-per-hectare-period-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=10}

  group_by(Year, Pasture_ID) %>%

  slice_max(Period_ID, n = 1L, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(
  production_by_pasture_period,
  aes(
    x = Period_ID,
    y = Gain_per_Hectare,
    group = interaction(Pasture_ID, Grazing_System),

) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.35, color = "grey55") +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.55, linewidth = 0.7) +

  ) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = SR), size = 2.9) +

    x = "RGP",
    y = paste0("Estimated gain per active hectare (", bw_unit_label, "/ha)"),
```

#### 5.7.2 Animal Performance Versus Land Productivity

The dashed lines are year-specific medians. Upper-right observations combine above-median animal ADG and above-median gain per hectare. Upper-left observations have relatively high land productivity despite lower individual-animal performance, often because of greater stocking density. Lower-right observations indicate good individual performance but comparatively low production per hectare.


#### 5.7.3 Documented-Period and Full-Window Seasonal Productivity

`Documented_Period_Gain_per_Pasture_Hectare` uses only the supplied rotation periods. `Full_Window_Gain_per_Pasture_Hectare` uses the complete requested body-weight window and the whole-pasture area in hectares, so it includes dates for which no rotation assignment was supplied.

```{r bw-seasonal-production-summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cumulative_pasture_production <- production_by_pasture_period %>%
  group_by(
    Year, Pasture_ID, Grazing_System, TRT, SR,
    Supplied_Pasture_Hectares
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    Documented_Periods = n_distinct(Period_ID),
    Documented_Days = sum(Period_Days),
    Estimated_Documented_Total_Gain = safe_sum_finite(
      Estimated_Total_Pasture_Gain
    ),
    Mean_Period_ADG = safe_mean_finite(Mean_Period_ADG),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Documented_Period_Gain_per_Pasture_Hectare =
      Estimated_Documented_Total_Gain / Supplied_Pasture_Hectares
  )

full_window_animal_grid <- production_animal_assignments %>%
  inner_join(analysis_windows_numeric, by = "Year")

full_window_animal_gain <- full_window_animal_grid %>%
  left_join(
    spline_predictions_production %>%
      transmute(
        Year, SEID,
        Start_Date = Date,
        Full_Start_BW = Fitted_BW
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "Start_Date")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    spline_predictions_production %>%
      transmute(
        Year, SEID,
        End_Date = Date,
        Full_End_BW = Fitted_BW
      ),
    by = c("Year", "SEID", "End_Date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Complete_Full_Window = is.finite(Full_Start_BW) &
      is.finite(Full_End_BW),
    Full_Window_Animal_Gain = if_else(
      Complete_Full_Window,
      Full_End_BW - Full_Start_BW,
      NA_real_
    ),
    Full_Window_ADG = Full_Window_Animal_Gain /
      as.integer(End_Date - Start_Date)
  )

full_window_pasture_production <- full_window_animal_gain %>%
  group_by(Year, Pasture_ID, TRT, SR) %>%
  summarise(
    Animals_Assigned = n_distinct(SEID),
    Animals_Complete = sum(Complete_Full_Window),
    Mean_Full_Window_Animal_Gain = safe_mean_finite(
      Full_Window_Animal_Gain
    ),
    Mean_Full_Window_ADG = safe_mean_finite(Full_Window_ADG),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Full_Window_Completeness_Percent = 100 *
      Animals_Complete / Animals_Assigned,
    Estimated_Full_Window_Total_Gain =
      Mean_Full_Window_Animal_Gain * Animals_Assigned
  ) %>%
  left_join(pasture_area_reference, by = "Pasture_ID") %>%
  mutate(
    Full_Window_Gain_per_Pasture_Hectare =
      Estimated_Full_Window_Total_Gain / Supplied_Pasture_Hectares
  )

seasonal_production_comparison <- cumulative_pasture_production %>%
  left_join(
    full_window_pasture_production %>%
      dplyr::select(
        Year, Pasture_ID,
        Full_Window_Completeness_Percent,
        Mean_Full_Window_ADG,
        Estimated_Full_Window_Total_Gain,
        Full_Window_Gain_per_Pasture_Hectare
      ),
    by = c("Year", "Pasture_ID")
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Pasture_ID)
```

### 5.8 Map Gain per Active Hectare for Every Period

Every pasture-period is represented by the dissolved HMM grid cells containing
grazing GPS fixes. Full pasture polygons are displayed only as spatial context.

```{r bw-attach-active-spatial-geometry, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
attach_active_geometry <- function(
  production_df,
  active_area_geometry_sf
) {
  active_geometry_keys <- active_area_geometry_sf %>%
    dplyr::rename(Period_ID = Rotation_Period) %>%
    dplyr::select(Year, Pasture_ID, Period_ID)

  unmatched_rows <- production_df %>%
    dplyr::anti_join(
      sf::st_drop_geometry(active_geometry_keys),
      by = c("Year", "Pasture_ID", "Period_ID")
    )

  if (nrow(unmatched_rows) > 0L) {
    stop(
      "At least one body-weight pasture-period could not be assigned its ",
      "HMM GPS-observed active-area geometry."
    )
  }

  result <- active_geometry_keys %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      production_df,
      by = c("Year", "Pasture_ID", "Period_ID")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Year, Period_ID, Pasture_ID)

  if (nrow(result) != nrow(production_df)) {
    stop("The body-weight active-geometry join changed the expected row count.")
  }

  result
}

period_production_sf <- attach_active_geometry(
  production_by_pasture_period,
  gps_active_area_geometry_sf
)

period_production_sf
```

### 5.9 Mixed models of active grazing area for both grids

The experimental unit is the pasture. The all-pasture and inside-assigned-RGP
grid scopes each have one pasture × year × RGP analysis. Whole-season area
has a single model of cells pooled across the full season. The RGP fixed effects are treatment × stocking rate × RGP; the
seasonal fixed effects are treatment × stocking rate. Both have pasture and
year random intercepts, following the user-requested specifications. The RGP
fit has no additional pasture-year intercept; within-season residual correlation
beyond Year/Pasture clustering remains a model limitation. The all-pasture seasonal
grid uses every observed grazing fix in the season window and counts a cell
once. The whole-season response is calculated directly from pooled GPS cells, never
by adding period areas or substituting an inside-RGP seasonal denominator.

There is one pasture per treatment × stocking combination and only three
years. Pasture and year intercepts account for repeated observations but
cannot create treatment replication. Full interaction contrasts are
conditional/descriptive; singularity and residual audits are exported.

```{r pasture-use-mixed-model, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# PASTURE ACTIVE-AREA DATASETS + MIXED MODELS
#
# Required spatial analyses:
#   1. RGP level: ALL_PASTURE_GRAZING
#   2. RGP level: INSIDE_RGP_GRAZING
#   3. Season level: WHOLE_SEASON_GRAZING
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Whole-season active area is calculated directly from the
# pooled seasonal grazing grid. It is NOT the sum/union of
# period-level inside-RGP areas.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Helper functions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

safe_percent <- function(num, den) {
  dplyr::if_else(
    is.finite(num) &
      is.finite(den) &
      den > 0,
    100 * num / den,
    NA_real_
  )
}

safe_mean <- function(x) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Check required columns
# ------------------------------------------------------------

required_active_cols <- c(
  "Year",
  "Pasture_ID",
  "TRT",
  "SR",
  "Rotation_Period",
  "Total_active_ha_period",
  "Active_ha_inside_rotation",
  "Pasture_area_ha"
)

missing_active_cols <- setdiff(
  required_active_cols,
  names(active_area_summary)
)

if (length(missing_active_cols) > 0) {
  stop(
    "active_area_summary is missing required columns: ",
    paste(missing_active_cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


required_season_cols <- c(
  "Year",
  "Pasture_ID",
  "Pasture_area_ha",
  "Season_unique_active_ha"
)

missing_season_cols <- setdiff(
  required_season_cols,
  names(season_active_summary)
)

if (length(missing_season_cols) > 0) {
  stop(
    "season_active_summary is missing required columns: ",
    paste(missing_season_cols, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Validate treatment and stocking labels BEFORE factor()
#    so unexpected labels are not silently converted to NA.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

trt_levels <- c(
  "Continuous",
  "Rotational"
)

sr_levels <- c(
  "Light",
  "Moderate",
  "Heavy"
)


observed_trt <- unique(
  stats::na.omit(
    as.character(active_area_summary$TRT)
  )
)

bad_trt <- setdiff(
  observed_trt,
  trt_levels
)

if (length(bad_trt) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Unexpected Treatment value(s): ",
    paste(bad_trt, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


observed_sr <- unique(
  stats::na.omit(
    as.character(active_area_summary$SR)
  )
)

bad_sr <- setdiff(
  observed_sr,
  sr_levels
)

if (length(bad_sr) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Unexpected Stocking value(s): ",
    paste(bad_sr, collapse = ", ")
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 3. PERIOD / RGP ACTIVE-AREA DATASET
# ============================================================

# First create a wide dataset so the spatial QC checks can
# directly compare all-pasture vs inside-RGP active hectares.

pasture_use_RGP_wide <- active_area_summary %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Year,
    Pasture_ID,
    TRT,
    SR,

    RGP = factor(
      paste0("RGP", Rotation_Period),
      levels = paste0("RGP", 1:5)
    ),

    active_ha_all_pasture =
      as.numeric(Total_active_ha_period),

    active_ha_inside_rgp =
      as.numeric(Active_ha_inside_rotation),

    Pasture_ha =
      as.numeric(Pasture_area_ha)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    pct_pasture_active_all = safe_percent(
      active_ha_all_pasture,
      Pasture_ha
    ),

    pct_pasture_active_inside_rgp = safe_percent(
      active_ha_inside_rgp,
      Pasture_ha
    ),

    Year = factor(Year),

    Pasture_ID = factor(Pasture_ID),

    TRT = factor(
      TRT,
      levels = trt_levels
    ),

    SR = factor(
      SR,
      levels = sr_levels
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RGP QC: duplicates
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (anyDuplicated(
  pasture_use_RGP_wide[
    c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID",
      "RGP"
    )
  ]
)) {
  stop(
    "Duplicate pasture-year-RGP record in ",
    "pasture_use_RGP_wide."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RGP QC: missing RGP
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (any(is.na(pasture_use_RGP_wide$RGP))) {

  bad_rgp <- pasture_use_RGP_wide %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.na(RGP))

  print(bad_rgp)

  stop(
    "At least one Rotation_Period could not be ",
    "converted to RGP1-RGP5."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RGP QC: negative active area
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (any(
  pasture_use_RGP_wide$active_ha_all_pasture < 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)) {
  stop(
    "Negative all-pasture active hectares detected."
  )
}


if (any(
  pasture_use_RGP_wide$active_ha_inside_rgp < 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)) {
  stop(
    "Negative inside-RGP active hectares detected."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RGP QC:
# inside-RGP active area must not exceed all-pasture area
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rgp_area_qc <- pasture_use_RGP_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(active_ha_inside_rgp),
    is.finite(active_ha_all_pasture),
    active_ha_inside_rgp >
      active_ha_all_pasture + 1e-5
  )

if (nrow(rgp_area_qc) > 0) {

  print(rgp_area_qc)

  stop(
    "Inside-RGP active area exceeds ",
    "all-pasture active area for at least one RGP."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RGP QC:
# active area cannot exceed total pasture area
# ------------------------------------------------------------

rgp_pasture_qc <- pasture_use_RGP_wide %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(active_ha_all_pasture),
    is.finite(Pasture_ha),
    active_ha_all_pasture >
      Pasture_ha + 1e-5
  )

if (nrow(rgp_pasture_qc) > 0) {

  print(rgp_pasture_qc)

  stop(
    "An RGP all-pasture active area ",
    "exceeds total pasture area."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Convert to long format for models and figures
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pasture_use_RGP <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  pasture_use_RGP_wide %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Year,
      Pasture_ID,
      TRT,
      SR,
      RGP,

      Grid_Map =
        "ALL_PASTURE_GRAZING",

      Active_ha =
        active_ha_all_pasture,

      Pasture_ha,

      Percent_pasture_active =
        pct_pasture_active_all
    ),

  pasture_use_RGP_wide %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Year,
      Pasture_ID,
      TRT,
      SR,
      RGP,

      Grid_Map =
        "INSIDE_RGP_GRAZING",

      Active_ha =
        active_ha_inside_rgp,

      Pasture_ha,

      Percent_pasture_active =
        pct_pasture_active_inside_rgp
    )
)


if (anyDuplicated(
  pasture_use_RGP[
    c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID",
      "RGP",
      "Grid_Map"
    )
  ]
)) {
  stop(
    "Duplicate pasture-year-RGP-grid record ",
    "in pasture_use_RGP."
  )
}


# ============================================================
# 4. WHOLE-SEASON ACTIVE-AREA DATASET
# ============================================================
#
# Do NOT calculate a seasonal inside-RGP union here.
#
# The required season denominator is:
#
#   Season_unique_active_ha
#
# calculated directly from all unique occupied grazing cells
# pooled across the entire pasture-year.
# ============================================================


season_trt_sr_lookup <- active_area_summary %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    Year,
    Pasture_ID,
    TRT,
    SR
  )


if (anyDuplicated(
  season_trt_sr_lookup[
    c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID"
    )
  ]
)) {

  duplicate_season_trt_sr <-
    season_trt_sr_lookup %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Year,
      Pasture_ID,
      name = "N"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(N > 1)

  print(duplicate_season_trt_sr)

  stop(
    "Treatment or stocking differs within ",
    "at least one pasture-year."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Keep optional season QC columns when they exist
# ------------------------------------------------------------

optional_season_cols <- intersect(
  c(
    "Season_calendar_days",
    "GPS_recorded_days_all_states",
    "Grazing_fixes_outside_RGP_calendar",
    "RGP_classified_fixes_within_pasture"
  ),
  names(season_active_summary)
)


season_grid_area <- season_active_summary %>%

  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::all_of(
      c(
        "Year",
        "Pasture_ID",
        "Pasture_area_ha",
        "Season_unique_active_ha",
        optional_season_cols
      )
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::left_join(
    season_trt_sr_lookup,
    by = c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID"
    ),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Make whole-season analysis dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pasture_use_season <- season_grid_area %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Grid_Map =
      "WHOLE_SEASON_GRAZING",

    Active_ha =
      as.numeric(Season_unique_active_ha),

    Pasture_ha =
      as.numeric(Pasture_area_ha),

      safe_percent(
        Active_ha,

      ),

    Year = factor(Year),

    Pasture_ID = factor(Pasture_ID),

    TRT = factor(
      TRT,
      levels = trt_levels
    ),

    SR = factor(
      SR,
      levels = sr_levels
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::select(
    Year,
    Pasture_ID,
    TRT,
    SR,
    Grid_Map,
    Active_ha,
    Pasture_ha,
    Percent_pasture_active,
    dplyr::all_of(optional_season_cols)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Season QC: one row per pasture-year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (anyDuplicated(
  pasture_use_season[
    c(
      "Year",
      "Pasture_ID"
    )
  ]
)) {
  stop(
    "Duplicate pasture-year whole-season record."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Season QC: missing treatment/stocking after join
# ------------------------------------------------------------

season_missing_design <- pasture_use_season %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.na(TRT) |
      is.na(SR)
  )

if (nrow(season_missing_design) > 0) {

  print(season_missing_design)

  stop(
    "Whole-season data contain missing ",
    "Treatment or Stocking after the join."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Season QC: active area cannot be negative
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (any(
  pasture_use_season$Active_ha < 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)) {
  stop(
    "Negative whole-season active hectares detected."
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Season QC: active area cannot exceed pasture
# ------------------------------------------------------------

season_pasture_qc <- pasture_use_season %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(Active_ha),
    is.finite(Pasture_ha),
    Active_ha >
      Pasture_ha + 1e-5

if (nrow(season_pasture_qc) > 0) {

  print(season_pasture_qc)

  stop(
    "Whole-season active area exceeds ",
    "total pasture area."
  )

# 5. SHOW EXACT ANALYSIS DATA AVAILABLE
# ============================================================

print(
  pasture_use_RGP %>%
    dplyr::count(
      Grid_Map,
      name = "N"

message("\nWhole-season grid counts:")

  pasture_use_season %>%
    dplyr::count(

      name = "N"
```
